title: Manchester City fans should direct anger at owners after guilty verdict
content:

The article notes that Mancini, who made millions from one of the “sham contracts” identified by a damning independent commission, viewed his role strictly as a hired expert. His departure left little regard for the legacy he left behind, reflecting a club culture driven by a win-at-all-costs attitude that circumvented regulatory rules.

While the Abu Dhabi regime’s success previously generated pride among supporters, the article argues that fans are justified in their anger and should direct it at the club’s owners. The text suggests that genuine feelings of pride can only be restored under new custodians, as the current leadership’s approach to hiring and financial management has fundamentally altered the club’s relationship with its fanbase.

content:

title: Jordan's giant desalination plant plan may lock in fossil gas use
content:
A proposed giant desalination plant in Jordan aims to address the country’s water scarcity, but the limited role of solar power in the energy-intensive project has raised concerns. Critics argue that the plan risks locking in demand for fossil gas, prompting questions about how climate adaptation finance is being allocated.

The project’s energy strategy has drawn scrutiny for its reliance on non-renewable sources despite the availability of solar power. This approach highlights tensions in climate adaptation efforts, where infrastructure built to combat water shortages may inadvertently increase carbon emissions.
summary: Jordan is planning a giant desalination plant to address water scarcity. The energy‑intensive project relies mainly on fossil gas, with only limited solar power, raising concerns about climate adaptation finance.

title: Matt Kean Criticizes NSW Planning Commission on Hunter Valley Coal Project
content:
Matt Kean, chair of the Climate Change Authority and a former New South Wales treasurer and energy minister, has criticized the state’s approval of the largest coal mining development in the state’s history. Kean, a senior climate adviser to the Albanese government, argued that “climate change isn’t someone else’s problem” and questioned the decision-making process behind the project’s green light.

The Hunter Valley Operations mine has been approved to operate until 2045. Kean stated that the state Independent Planning Commission did not account for the economic damage related to climate change caused by burning the coal from the mine. He specifically challenged why the commission failed to weigh these economic costs before granting approval.
summary: Matt Kean, chair of the Climate Change Authority, criticized the Independent Planning Commission for not considering climate-related economic damage in approving the Hunter Valley Operations mine, the largest coal project in NSW history. He questioned why the commission allowed the mine to run until 2045 without weighing the economic cost of burning the coal.

content: California Governor Gavin Newsom said that former President Donald Trump is a “gift” to the climate cause, arguing that Trump has become an environmentalist. title: Vineland NJ datacenter emitted large pollution for almost a year before regulators stepped in
content:
DataOne, a Microsoft-linked datacenter in Vineland, New Jersey, emitted substantial amounts of health-harming air pollution for nearly a year before state regulators intervened, according to public records obtained by Floodlight. The facility’s 62 gas-fired generators were revealed in August following a visual investigation by Floodlight and The Guardian, which determined that the equipment was operating without permits.

The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection recently fined the company $1 million for operating the unpermitted fleet of generators. However, the department did not disclose the specific duration the generators had been in operation or the total volume of air pollution released into the surrounding community over the past year.
summary: Vineland, New Jersey, DataOne datacenter emitted large amounts of health-harming air pollution for nearly a year before state regulators stepped in. The company was fined $1 million for running unpermitted generators, but the department did not disclose how long the generators had been operating or how much pollution was released.

summary: Donald Trump repeatedly claimed Americans flush toilets 10 to 15 times more than once. He made the remarks in 2019 and again at a Michigan rally in 2020.

content:

title: Damaged Mitochondria May Contribute to Liver Disease, Researchers Say
content:
Researchers at the Institute of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology I at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) and University Hospital Düsseldorf (UKD) are investigating how damaged mitochondria may contribute to liver disease.  

Mitochondria supply cells with energy and play an important role in metabolism. The research team is studying the role of mitochondria in the development of certain diseases, with a focus on liver pathology.  

The study aims to clarify the impact of mitochondrial dysfunction on liver disease.
summary: Mitochondria provide energy to cells and are important for metabolism. Researchers at the Institute of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology I at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and University Hospital Düsseldorf are studying how mitochondria contribute to the development of certain diseases.

title: Faith leaders willing to partner on hypertension screenings, study finds
content:
Faith leaders offer untapped key to hypertension crisis, research shows

A new study has found that faith leaders are willing to partner on hypertension screenings and education. The research highlights their potential role in addressing the hypertension crisis.

The study notes that, despite challenges in past health collaborations, faith leaders remain open to working with health professionals to promote blood‑pressure awareness and screening initiatives. Their involvement could help reach communities that have been underserved by traditional medical outreach.

The findings suggest that engaging faith leaders may provide a valuable avenue for improving hypertension prevention and management.

title: Standardized ICU Discharge Readiness Process Aims to Reduce Readmissions
content:
Initiative standardizes evaluation of ICU discharge readiness

A new initiative introduces a standardized process for assessing patients’ readiness to leave the intensive care unit (ICU). The goal is to reduce readmissions and provide clearer guidance for care teams.

According to a study published in Critical Care Nurse, the standardized evaluation helps lower readmission rates while fostering collaboration among the interprofessional team. The process offers a consistent framework for determining when patients are ready for transfer out of the ICU.
summary: A study published in Critical Care Nurse describes a standardized process for evaluating patients' readiness to leave the ICU. The process is said to reduce readmissions, provide clarity, and support collaboration among the interprofessional team.

title: Brain connectivity reveals new insights for personalized psychiatry in depression
content:
A research team from the Sant Pau Research Institute (IR Sant Pau) has published a review that calls for a paradigm shift in how depression is understood and studied.  

The review argues that the field should move beyond traditional psychiatric diagnoses that rely on broad categories. Instead, it advocates a dimensional approach that focuses on specific symptoms and their underlying neurobiological mechanisms.  

By emphasizing symptom‑specific and neurobiological insights, the authors suggest a more personalized framework for psychiatric research and treatment of depression.
summary: A review by a research team from the Sant Pau Research Institute proposes a paradigm shift in how depression is understood and studied. The study calls for moving beyond traditional broad psychiatric categories toward a dimensional approach that focuses on specific symptoms and their underlying neurobiological mechanisms.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AI software could detect osteoporosis in existing CT scans before bones break
content:
AI software could detect osteoporosis in existing CT scans before bones break

Osteoporosis progresses gradually and painlessly over many years, and many people do not have their bone density measured until they break a bone or develop back pain. By then, bone loss is usually already well advanced.

In the BMDNow joint research project, researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Computer Graphics Research IGD are collaborating closely with Goethe University Frankfurt and IT company Garritz Online Media International to develop software that helps detect osteoporosis at an early stage, before fractures occur.
summary: Osteoporosis progresses gradually and painlessly over many years. Many people do not have their bone density measured until they break a bone or develop back pain.

title: Walmart rolls out light-up digital shelf labels linked to its app
content:
Walmart is rolling out a new light‑up digital shelf label feature to help shoppers and employees locate items more easily. The labels are linked to the company's app, allowing customers to see which products are in stock and where they are located in the store.  

The initiative is intended to improve the shopping experience by making it easier for customers to find the items they need. By using the app to view the illuminated shelf labels, shoppers can quickly identify product locations and reduce time spent searching.  

Walmart’s rollout of the light‑up shelf labels is part of the retailer’s ongoing efforts to enhance in‑store navigation for both customers and staff.
summary: Walmart is rolling out a light-up shelf label feature. The labels are connected to Walmart’s app to help customers find items.

title: US borrowing costs hit highest since 2002 as UK 30‑year bond yield reaches 6%
content:
A global bond rout has begun again, with UK 30‑year gilt yields reaching their highest level since 1998. The market is also witnessing a widening risk premium between French and German government bonds, the spread climbing to 127.51 basis points after peaking at 128.80 basis points – the highest since June 2012.

Inflation, fiscal deficits and increased issuance are cited as key pressures on the bond market. Investors are reluctant to enter the market until a clearer sense of stability emerges, leading to a “buyers strike” on the trading floor. Hedge funds have suffered in the latest sell‑off and lack the appetite to support the move.

Real‑money investors may retain some risk appetite, but they too are waiting for stability before stepping in.
summary: U.S. government borrowing costs have risen to their highest level since 2002, while the UK 30‑year gilt yield has reached 6%, the highest since 1998. The spread between French and German government bond yields widened to 127.51 bps, the largest gap since June 2012, and investors are hesitant to enter the market, with hedge funds showing reduced risk appetite.

title: Scientists study pear, football, and Frisbee shapes of exotic nuclei
content:
Exploring the shapes of exotic nuclei

In the conventional diagram of an atom, the center depicts a nucleus—a spherical cluster of protons and neutrons. That sphere is a simplification.  

Nuclei can deform into exotic shapes that appear more like a pear, football or Frisbee.  

Understanding why and when nuclei distort is crucial for predicting and modeling how they will behave.
summary: Nuclei, normally depicted as spherical clusters of protons and neutrons, can deform into exotic shapes such as pear, football, or Frisbee. Understanding when and why these distortions occur is essential for predicting and modeling nuclear behavior.

title: Mars May Have Experienced Ancient Rain, Suggesting Life‑Related Chemistry
content:
The Mars we know today is a cold, dry world of dust and rocks. However, around 3.8–3.6 billion years ago, it may have looked very different.

Geological and mineral evidence suggests that, in its distant past, the planet experienced periods warm and wet enough for water to exist on its surface, potentially forming rivers, lakes and even an ocean in the northern hemisphere.
summary: Mars is currently a cold, dry world of dust and rocks. Geological and mineral evidence indicates that between 3.8 and 3.6 billion years ago, the planet had warm, wet periods that could have produced rivers, lakes, and an ocean in the northern hemisphere.
author: Phys.org

title: Cogongrass adds fuel to hotter Florida wildfires
content:
Florida wildfires are burning hotter and spreading faster, raising concerns about the factors driving the increased intensity and reach of the blazes.  

A study conducted by the University of Florida points to cogongrass, an invasive grass that has spread across much of Florida and the southeastern United States, as a key contributor. The research suggests that cogongrass adds more fuel to the landscape, helping fires to ignite more rapidly and travel farther.
summary: A University of Florida study says cogongrass is adding fuel to Florida wildfires. The invasive grass has spread across Florida and the southeastern United States.

title: East Anglia study shows Letter Swap platform modernizes adoption communication
content:
Digital technology is poised to change how adopted children maintain contact with their birth families, a new study from the University of East Anglia suggests. The research, published in the journal Adoption & Fostering, examines the potential of online tools to enhance communication beyond traditional methods.

The study highlights a custom-built online platform called Letter Swap, which allows families to exchange messages, videos, voice notes and photos. By offering these modern communication options, Letter Swap provides a more dynamic and immediate way for adopted children and their birth families to stay connected, moving away from the reliance on annual letters.

The findings indicate that digital platforms like Letter Swap could offer families richer, more frequent opportunities for interaction, potentially strengthening relationships between adopted children and their birth families.
summary: A study from the University of East Anglia published in Adoption & Fostering shows that the Letter Swap platform lets adopted children connect with birth families by exchanging messages, videos, voice notes and photos. The platform offers modern communication options instead of traditional annual letters.
author: Phys.org

title: Eye-eating amoeba resists treatment; biochemistry study may help
content:
Eye‑eating amoeba resists treatment—understanding its biochemistry could help

A free‑living, single‑cell organism called Acanthamoeba lives in water, soil and air. Most of the time it keeps to itself, but on rare occasions it can infect humans and cause severe infections of the eyes, skin and even the brain.

The eye infection, known as Acanthamoeba keratitis, is difficult for doctors to diagnose and treat. The organism resists conventional treatment, and scientists believe that a deeper understanding of its biochemistry may improve therapeutic options.
summary: Acanthamoeba is a free‑living single‑cell organism found in water, soil and air that can rarely infect humans, causing severe eye, skin, and brain infections. The eye infection, Acanthamoeba keratitis, is difficult for doctors to diagnose and treat.
author: Phys.org

title: Consortium Maps Mitochondrial Proteins in Plant and Five Pathogens
content:
A research consortium has produced the broadest catalog yet of the proteins that compose mitochondria, uncovering unusual functions across the tree of complex life.  

The study captures mitochondrial diversity across multiple branches, with major contributions from scientists at the Broad Institute and its Proteomics Platform.  

The consortium generated and analyzed mitochondrial proteomes from one plant species and five single‑cellular pathogens that affect millions of people worldwide each year.  

The work provides the most extensive view to date of mitochondrial protein composition.
summary: A research consortium produced the most comprehensive catalog of mitochondrial proteins, covering a plant and five single‑cell pathogens. The work was led by Broad Institute scientists and its Proteomics Platform, providing insights into organelle diversity across the tree of complex life.
author: Phys.org

title: Chimpanzees Prefer Certain Peers for Grooming and Food Sharing
content:
Scientists have found that chimpanzees favor certain peers by grooming them selectively and sharing food only with chosen companions. The animals also plunder less pineapple from friends and expect the same reciprocity in return.  

This selective behavior offers a glimpse into humanity’s prosocial evolutionary past.  

A question that remains is how a chimpanzee friendship might influence antisocial acts.
summary: Scientists have shown that chimpanzees favor certain peers by choosing whom to groom and selectively sharing food. The behavior offers insight into humanity's prosocial evolutionary past, but researchers question how friendships might affect antisocial acts.

title: Study shows citywide fire data masks block-level trends in NYC
content:
Study finds city-level fire data can hide what's happening block by block

A new study of a decade of New York City fire data shows that citywide trends can mask sharply different realities on the ground. While aggregate statistics suggest overall patterns, the research reveals that individual neighborhoods may be experiencing trends that run counter to the city’s average.

The analysis indicates that some neighborhoods are moving in the opposite direction of the city as a whole, highlighting the importance of examining fire data at a more granular level.
summary: A decade of New York City fire data reveals that citywide trends can hide block-level differences. Some neighborhoods are trending opposite to the citywide trend.

title: Protective Fabric Plant Armor Boosts Strawberry Yields 3.56‑fold
content:
New “plant armor” more than triples strawberry yields

A new protective fabric, called Plant Armor, has increased strawberry yields by as much as 3.56 times. The material blocks insects while still allowing sunlight, rain, and airflow to reach the plants.

Originally inspired by research on military clothing, Plant Armor could also help farms reduce pesticide and water use.
summary: The protective fabric, called Plant Armor, increased strawberry yields by up to 3.56 times while blocking insects. It allows sunlight, rain, and airflow to reach the plants and was inspired by military clothing research, which could help farms reduce pesticide and water use.
author: Science Daily

title: Superfluid Helium Qubit Could Cut Quantum Error Rates 100×
content:
A new qubit design using superfluid helium has been proposed that could reduce quantum computing error rates by about 100 times. The reduction would come from shielding quantum information from common forms of electromagnetic noise.

If experimental tests confirm the predictions, the superfluid helium qubit could be integrated alongside today’s superconducting qubits. It might also function as a new type of quantum memory.
summary: A proposed qubit made with superfluid helium could reduce quantum computing error rates by about 100 times by shielding information from electromagnetic noise. If experiments confirm the predictions, the technology could work alongside superconducting qubits or serve as a new quantum memory.
author: Science Daily

title: Giant Australian Stick Insect Misidentified for Decades, Scientists Find Two New Species
content:
Scientists have identified two new species of large Australian stick insects, one of which lays extraordinary “lidded” eggs that have never before been recorded in the group.  

The discovery also revealed that a familiar stick insect had been misidentified for decades, underscoring how much biodiversity may still be hiding in plain sight.
summary: Scientists identified two new species of large Australian stick insects, one of which lays extraordinary “lidded” eggs never before recorded in the group. The discovery also revealed that a familiar stick insect had been misidentified for decades, showing how much biodiversity may still be hiding in plain sight.
author: Science Daily

title: APOE4 gene may damage brain vessels but some effects reversed in lab studies
content:
Scientists have discovered that the Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins.  

In laboratory experiments, researchers were able to reverse some of these effects. The reversal revealed promising new targets for Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and other neurodegenerative diseases.  

These findings point to potential therapeutic avenues for conditions linked to APOE4.
summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins. Researchers were able to reverse some of these effects in experiments, revealing promising new targets for Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and other neurodegenerative diseases.
author: Science Daily

title: MIND Diet Linked to 2.5-Year Delay in Brain Aging
content:
Individuals who adhered closely to the MIND diet experienced slower brain shrinkage and reduced grey matter loss over time. The most significant differences observed between groups were equivalent to approximately 2.5 years of delayed brain aging.

Specific dietary components were linked to distinct outcomes in brain health. Berries and poultry were associated with healthier brain changes, whereas sweets and fried fast foods were connected to greater tissue loss.
summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely experienced slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time. The greatest differences were equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging, with berries and poultry linked to healthier brain changes and sweets and fried fast foods linked to greater tissue loss.
author: Science Daily

title: WHO Announces Reversible Male Contraceptives Could Reach Market in 5–10 Years
content:
The World Health Organization announced last week that it expects reversible male hormonal contraceptives to be available on the market within five to 10 years. This development marks a significant shift in a field where progress has historically been slow; since the first vasectomy in the 1890s, the only other major reversible method added to the male contraceptive repertoire was the rubber condom, which entered the mass market in the 1850s.

Other news items include senior Downing Street officials contacting thinktanks and pollsters to gauge public support for the UK rejoining the EU. In the Middle East, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that a pilot on a flight from the United Arab Emirates to Israel stabbed his co-pilot and attempted to crash the aircraft, with officials investigating the incident as a potential terror attack. Additionally, Andy Burnham indicated there are “strong indications” that Iran played a role in events leading to the arrest of five men near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire during a terror investigation.

The UK government’s “one in one out” deal with France, intended to deter small boat arrivals, is expected to expire on Thursday as negotiations stall over French demands for an EU-wide scheme. In television news, Esther Rantzen, the Bafta-winning presenter and founder of Childline, has died aged 86, with her family paying tribute to her as a “most wonderful mother” and “cherished grandmother.”
summary: The World Health Organization announced that reversible male contraceptives may be available on the market within five to ten years. The announcement follows a long history of slow progress in male contraceptive development since the first vasectomy in the 1890s.
author: Guardian Science

title: Astrologers Debated Authority at Largest Global Conference in Chicago
content:
Astrology has grown into a $15 billion industry in the United States, reaching new levels of mainstream popularity. Despite this expansion, practitioners continue to debate who holds authority over the interpretation of celestial bodies. These discussions were evident at the United Astrology Conference, described as the largest professional gathering of astrologers in the world, held in downtown Chicago.

The event attracted 1,500 attendees who navigated a marketplace of vendors selling books, tracts, affiliations, proprietary apps, and software programs. These digital tools have largely replaced the traditional, labor-intensive process of drawing charts by hand. During the conference, one participant emphasized the significance of dwarf planets, stating that they "change everything."
summary: The United Astrology Conference, the world's largest professional gathering of astrologers, drew about 1,500 attenders in downtown Chicago, as the $15bn industry becomes more mainstream. Vendors sold books, tracts, affiliations, proprietary apps and software that replace traditional chart drawing, while astrologers debated who has authority over celestial bodies, with one speaker noting that dwarf planets change everything.
author: Guardian Science

title: Steve Ramirez discusses memory manipulation science in podcast
content:
Madeleine Finlay interviews Steve Ramirez, an associate professor of psychological and brain sciences at Boston University, on a new podcast episode. Ramirez’s book, How to Change a Memory, was recently shortlisted for this year’s Royal Society Trivedi science book prize.

During the discussion, Ramirez explains how scientists have successfully located memories in the brains of rodents, artificially triggered them, and removed them. He also outlines the potential practical applications of this research for humans in the future.
summary: Steve Ramirez, an associate professor of psychological and brain sciences at Boston University, discusses his book "How to Change a Memory" in a podcast. He explains how scientists have located, triggered, and removed memories in rodents and explores potential human applications.
author: Guardian Science

title: Scottish island Lismore excavations find sixth-century monastery
content:
Community-funded archaeological excavations on the Scottish island of Lismore have uncovered findings described as “hugely exciting,” shedding new light on the spread of Christianity and rewriting the history of the site. The island, located near Oban in Argyll and home to a population of 190, was the site of a sixth-century AD monastic settlement established during the period when Irish missionaries were moving into northern Britain.

Prior to these recent discoveries, physical evidence from this era was limited to a few fragments of an early carved cross. The excavations of the monastery, characterized as “really important,” have provided new insights into the community life and historical significance of the island, which today features a Gaelic heritage centre that records its long history.
summary: Community-funded archaeological excavations on the Scottish island of Lismore have uncovered a sixth-century monastery. These finds shed light on the spread of Christianity and rewrite the historical story of the island.
author: Guardian Science

title: Webb Observes Collisions That Shaped Early Solar System
content:
NASA’s Webb telescope has delivered a concise overview of planet‑shattering collisions. Scientists theorize that in the early history of our solar system a Mars‑sized object called Theia struck the infant Earth, vaporizing vast amounts of rock and blasting it into space.

Some of the ejected material coalesced into the Moon. The Moon is now the focus of NASA’s Artemis program, which is returning humans, preparing for Mars, and shaping the future of space.
summary: NASA's Webb telescope is providing data on planet-shattering collisions in the early solar system. Scientists theorize a Mars-sized object named Theia struck infant Earth, creating material that coalesced into the Moon.
author: NASA News

title: Michael Sheen's campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing
content:
Michael Sheen’s campaign on toxic waste sites has secured backing from the Senedd, marking a significant political endorsement for the effort to address contaminated land across Wales.

All parties have urged Welsh and UK ministers to ensure that polluters pay to clean up contaminated land, emphasizing the need for accountability and remediation of hazardous sites.
summary: All parties have urged Welsh and UK ministers to ensure polluters pay to clean up contaminated land. This follows Michael Sheen's campaign on toxic waste sites gaining backing in the Senedd.
author: BBC Science

title: Scottish Government Expands Bluetongue Restriction Zone to All of Scotland
content:
The Scottish government has announced that the Bluetongue restriction zone will be expanded to cover the entirety of Scotland. The decision is intended to streamline operations for those affected by the current regional restrictions.

Officials stated that this change will simplify trading processes for farmers, hauliers, and auction markets.
summary: The Scottish government announced an expansion of the Bluetongue restriction zone to cover all of Scotland. The move is intended to simplify trading for farmers, hauliers, and auction markets.
author: BBC Science

content: Micron’s Chief Executive Officer stated that memory supply conditions are expected to become significantly tighter in 2027 and 2028 compared to the current year, 2026. summary: Micron CEO announced that memory supply will be tighter in 2027 and 2028 compared to 2026. The announcement was reported on TechPowerUp.

content:

content:
Law enforcement officers can now bypass the automatic reboot feature on iPhones to access locked devices, according to a report by 404 Media. The story has generated discussion on the Hacker News platform, where it received 18 points and 2 comments.

title: Smaller distributed batteries could help the grid amid NYC regulation hurdles
content:
How smaller, distributed batteries could help the grid

Installing a large battery in New York City requires navigating a notoriously tough tangle of regulations, making it difficult to bring large energy storage projects onto the grid. In response to these obstacles, some startups are turning to smaller batteries, deploying them in unexpected places to provide distributed storage solutions.
summary: Large battery projects in New York City face tough regulations, making grid storage difficult. Startups are using smaller batteries in unexpected places to overcome these obstacles.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: AI tool reconstructs images from brain scans
content:
A new AI tool can infer what a person is looking at by analyzing their brain scans and then recreate that image with remarkable precision. The system also works in reverse, predicting a person's brain activity based on the visual stimulus they are viewing.

In the accompanying image, the left‑hand image of each pair is shown as an example of the visual input used for the analysis. The right‑hand image demonstrates the reconstructed view generated by the AI.
summary: A new AI tool can guess what you’re looking at by analyzing brain scans and re-create that image with remarkable precision. It can also predict a person’s brain activity based on what they’re looking at.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: AI “mind-reading” tool can reconstruct images from brain scans
content:
A new AI tool can reconstruct what a person is looking at by analyzing their brain scans. The technology, described in this week’s edition of The Download, is being promoted as a form of “mind‑reading” that decodes visual content directly from neural activity.

According to the newsletter, the tool can guess what a viewer is seeing by processing the brain scan data. The article notes that the AI can reconstruct the image that the subject is viewing.
summary: An AI “mind-reading” tool can reconstruct what you’re looking at based on a brain scan. The new AI tool can guess what you’re looking at just by analyzing your brain scans.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Expert Robert A. Pape says mainstream Americans, not fringe, pose violence threat to midterms
content:
Robert A. Pape, a leading authority on political violence, warns that the greatest danger to the upcoming midterm elections is not extremist fringe groups but ordinary Americans who view violence as a viable response.  

Pape says the threat is emerging from the mainstream, urging the public to recognize that regular citizens contemplating violent action pose the real risk to the electoral process.
summary: Robert A. Pape, a leading authority on political violence, says the threat to the midterms comes from mainstream Americans who see violence as an answer, not from fringe groups. He urges Americans to recognize this risk.
author: Wired

title: Best Gifts for Parents and Their Babies: Bottle Washers, Prepared Meals, and More
content:
Best Gifts for Parents (and Their Babies): Bottle Washers, Prepared Meals, and More

A new guide highlights practical gifts for parents navigating the early stages of newborn care. The focus is on items that ease daily tasks, such as bottle washers and prepared meals.

The article suggests that these gifts and gadgets can significantly help parents who are deep into newborn survival, making parenting a little easier.
summary: These gifts and gadgets can help ease parenting for a friend in newborn survival. The list includes bottle washers, prepared meals, and other items.

title: US Measles Resurgence Forces Hospitals to Adopt New Protocols
content:
Measles Is Forcing Hospitals to Adapt to a New Normal

The resurgence of measles in the United States is prompting hospitals and health systems to adopt new protocols and procedures. Health facilities that previously considered measles a historical concern are now revising their practices to manage the disease’s reemergence.
summary: The US resurgence of measles is forcing hospitals and health systems to adopt new protocols and procedures. The disease was previously thought to be in the past.
author: Wired

title: Two Driverless Cars Crash at 155 mph on Formula 1 Track
content: Two driverless cars crashed while racing at speeds of 155 mph, and only two of the five autonomous vehicles finished the race around a notoriously difficult Formula 1 track. The incidents highlighted how autonomous systems can struggle with blind corners, sensor failures, and the physics of high‑speed racing. The crashes underscored the challenges of deploying self‑driving technology in environments that demand rapid decision‑making and precise navigation.
summary: Only two of five driverless vehicles finished the race around a notoriously difficult Formula 1 track. The crashes exposed issues with autonomous systems encountering blind corners, sensor failures, and physics.
author: Wired

title: Amazon Refreshes Kindle, Paperwhite, Colorsoft Line for 20th Anniversary
content: Amazon is set to update its entire Kindle e‑reader lineup ahead of the device’s 20th anniversary next year. The refresh will feature new color options, an aluminum construction, and a redesigned frame that is both thinner and lighter than previous models.
summary: Amazon is updating its entire e-reader range ahead of the Kindle’s 20th anniversary. The new models feature fresh colors, an aluminum build, and a thinner, lighter frame design.
author: Wired

title: Amazon launches colorful new Kindle models with aluminum options and page‑turn buttons
content:
Amazon announced the launch of next‑generation Kindle devices, adding new color options and a case with physical page‑turn buttons. The lineup includes the base Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft, each a millimeter thinner than previous models and 30 percent faster at opening books.

The devices’ power buttons have been relocated from the bottom to the right edge near the top. They are offered in vibrant new colors with a soft‑touch plastic case, and for the first time customers can choose a few aluminum shades, which provide a higher‑end look and double the storage capacity of the plastic versions—32 GB versus 16 GB. Amazon’s Kindle vice president, Kevin Keith, discussed the updates.
summary: Amazon is releasing next‑generation base Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft that are a millimeter thinner, 30% faster at opening books, and have power buttons moved to the right edge near the top. They ship in vibrant colors with a soft‑touch plastic case that includes physical page‑turn buttons, and optional aluminum finishes that double storage to 32 GB from 16 GB.
author: The Verge

title: Gears of War: E-Day praised as strong prequel despite untimely launch
content:
Gears of War: E‑Day, a prequel to one of Xbox’s most transformative titles, has arrived as a new action game that emphasizes a brutal, tense and self‑aware experience. The game sticks closely to its premise, delivering the series’ signature up‑close cover‑shooter gameplay that remains distinct even twenty years after the original Gears of War debuted.

The Verge notes that E‑Day demonstrates the franchise’s continued impact, “still hits hard two decades later,” and suggests the title may offer an early glimpse of Xbox’s direction as the platform moves into a “messy new era focused on its biggest franchises.” Despite its strengths, the release is occurring at a time described as “terrible,” according to the article’s headline.
summary: Gears of War: E-Day is a prequel to the original Gears of War that delivers a brutal, tense and self‑aware action experience. The game is launching during a messy new era for Xbox as the company focuses on its biggest franchises.
author: The Verge

title: Samsung hikes US price of base Galaxy S26 to nearly $1,000
content:
Samsung has raised the price of its base Galaxy S26 with 256 GB of storage in the United States by $100 or more, bringing the cost to nearly $1,000, Phone Arena reports.

The Galaxy S26 and S26 Plus were already $100 more expensive than their S25 predecessors when they launched earlier this year, a hike Samsung said was partly due to rising RAM costs. With the latest increase, the base S26 now costs $200 more than the base S25 would have, and nearly every model in the S26 lineup is $100 pricier on Samsung’s official website, with the 1 TB version of the S26 Ultra seeing an even larger rise. Apple and Google have also raised phone prices this year.

The price adjustments are reflected on Samsung’s U.S. website, and the full story is available at The Verge.
summary: The base 256 GB Galaxy S26 now costs nearly $1,000 in the United States after Samsung raised its price by $100 or more. Combined with an earlier $100 increase over the S25, the base S26 is $200 more expensive than the base S25 would have been.
author: The Verge

title: RoseBerry Media to recut Neighbours episodes into microdramas for Epis platform
content:
RoseBerry Media announced that it will re‑edit episodes of the Australian soap opera Neighbours into short “microdrama” clips for the vertical‑video platform Epis, Variety reported on Monday. The clips will be drawn from two storylines that aired in the late 2000s and feature a character portrayed by Margot Robbie.

Neighbours, which aired for 41 seasons from 1985 to 2025, is being repackaged for short‑form viewing. RoseBerry co‑founder and CEO Guy Hameiri said the series is “an iconic piece of television history” that is well suited to adaptation for vertical viewing. The microdramas will be the first content released under the project.
summary: RoseBerry Media is recutting episodes of the Australian soap Neighbours into short vertical “microdramas” that will be released on the Epis streaming platform. The launch will initially feature two late‑aughts storylines focused on a character played by Margot Robbie, and cofounder / CEO Guy Hameiri called the show an iconic piece of television history suited to vertical viewing.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI unveils Dots AI agent at DevDay 2026, targeting Meta's Muse platform
content:
OpenAI unveiled a new personal‑assistant agent called Dots at its annual DevDay conference in 2026. CEO Sam Altman introduced the “real‑deal AI” agent, which runs on the GPT‑6 Astra model and is “inspired by the cool agents that we all watched in movies growing up,” according to the company’s presentation.

Dots is designed to resemble the colorful, customizable blobs with eyes that characterize Meta’s Muse AI platform, which has achieved early success. OpenAI highlighted Dots’ ability to go beyond typical assistance tasks by generating metaverse‑style virtual worlds during the live demo.

A pop‑up shop for Dots was displayed at the DevDay event, and the launch was accompanied by a photo from Heather Diehl/Getty Images. The Verge reported on the announcement.
summary: At OpenAI's annual DevDay 2026, CEO Sam Altman introduced Dots, a "real‑deal AI" agent powered by GPT‑6 Astra. Dots, a colorful personalizable blob with eyes, is presented as a competitor to Meta's Muse AI platform and was shown building virtual‑world environments.
author: The Verge

title: NYC enacts click-to-cancel rule, first US city to ban hard-to-cancel subscriptions
content:
New York City has begun enforcing a “click‑to‑cancel” rule that requires businesses to make ending a subscription as simple as signing up for one. The regulation, which took effect on Thursday, allows residents to submit complaints to the city government if they encounter difficulties canceling recurring fees.

Under the rule, companies such as gyms that permit online enrollment may no longer require customers to call or visit a physical location to terminate a membership. The city’s enforcement marks the first time the rule has been applied anywhere in the United States, after an appeals court dismissed a similar federal proposal on procedural grounds.

City officials estimate the policy could save New Yorkers between $21.5 million and $162.5 million each year. The story was reported by The Verge.
summary: New York City’s click-to-cancel rule requires businesses to make canceling a subscription as easy as signing up. The city, the first municipality where the rule has taken effect after a federal version was struck down, expects annual savings of $21.5 million to $162.5 million.
author: The Verge

title: NASA squeezes Treasury, vibe coded, breaks mold to save Swift
content:
NASA employed an unconventional approach, described as “squeezing” the Treasury, using “vibe coding,” and breaking the usual mold in an effort to save the Swift mission.  

A spokesperson for the effort said, “We did some really, really cool stuff. I’m absolutely gutted we weren’t able to get further.”  

The initiative, however, did not progress beyond its initial stage.
summary: NASA squeezed the Treasury, vibe coded and broke the mold in an effort to save Swift. A person said they did some really cool stuff but were gutted they weren’t able to get further.
author: Ars Technica

title: PS5 emulation makes big strides on PC as Astro Bot, Demon’s Souls run
content:
PS5 emulation on personal computers is reportedly making significant progress, according to recent observations.  

Developers and users have noted that titles such as Astro Bot and Demon’s Souls are now running ably on PC hardware without the need for a PlayStation 5 console.  

The ability to play these games on non‑console systems highlights a rapid improvement in PS5 emulation capabilities.
summary: PS5 emulation is making big strides on PC. Games such as Astro Bot and Demon’s Souls are running ably without a console.
author: Ars Technica

title: Satlyt raises $8M to develop open AI software for satellites
content:
Satlyt, a startup founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, announced it has raised $8 million to develop artificial‑intelligence capabilities for satellites.

The company says it aims to become the “Android of orbital computing,” providing open software that can run on satellites from multiple operators, in contrast to SpaceX’s closed, all‑in‑one iPhone‑style system.
summary: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, announced an $8 million funding round. The company aims to offer open orbital‑computing software that runs AI on multiple satellites, positioning itself as an Android‑like alternative to SpaceX’s closed approach.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon launches Kindle Click, a $35 Bluetooth remote for hands‑free page turning
content:
Amazon has launched Kindle Click, a compact Bluetooth remote priced at $35. The device is intended for Kindle users who want to turn pages without physically handling the e‑reader.

Kindle Click connects wirelessly to the Kindle and allows readers to flip pages by pressing a button on the remote, offering a hands‑free reading experience.
summary: Amazon introduced the Kindle Click, a compact Bluetooth remote priced at $35. It is designed to let readers turn pages without touching their Kindle.

title: New Kindle removes raised bezel, becoming smaller and lighter
content:
Amazon’s latest Kindle models have removed the traditional raised bezel, aiming for a smaller and lighter e‑reader.  

The new lineup is described as the lightest and thinnest in the series, featuring a front‑flush display that eliminates bezels entirely.  

The design change reflects a push toward a more streamlined, portable reading device.
summary: The new Kindle lineup removes the raised bezel, adopting a front‑flush display. The redesign makes the device its lightest and thinnest model yet, aiming for a smaller, lighter e‑reader.

title: Audible adds features to track characters, explore settings, and chat with AI characters
content:
Audible is introducing a suite of new features designed to deepen listeners’ engagement with audiobooks. The updates allow users to keep track of characters, explore locations and imagery referenced in the narratives, and interact directly with characters.

The character‑tracking tools let listeners identify and follow individuals throughout a story, while the exploration functions provide contextual information about places and visual details mentioned in the text. Additionally, Audible is incorporating generative‑AI technology that enables users to converse with book characters in real time.

These enhancements aim to create a more immersive listening experience by blending traditional audiobook content with interactive, AI‑driven capabilities.
summary: Audible is rolling out new features that let listeners keep track of characters and explore places and imagery mentioned in books. The features also enable users to interact with characters using generative AI.
author: TechCrunch

title: Photon raises $4.5M to replace mobile apps with AI agents on messaging platforms
content:
Photon, a startup focused on AI‑driven communication tools, announced a symbolic “funeral for mobile apps” as it pivots toward building AI agents that operate within messaging services. The company has secured $4.5 million in funding to develop agents that function over iMessage, SMS/RCS, email and other platforms.

Photon’s new strategy bets on consumers favoring these messaging‑based agents over traditional app downloads, offering developers a way to create AI assistants that reach users directly through the channels they already use.
summary: Photon, a startup, has $4.5 million to build AI agents that operate over iMessage, SMS/RCS, email and other messaging platforms. The funding supports its plan to replace traditional mobile apps as consumers shift to using agents instead of downloading apps.
author: TechCrunch

title: Brian Chesky says AI agents need their own operating system
content: Brian Chesky discussed the need for a dedicated operating system for AI agents in a recent interview. He highlighted efforts to make Airbnb more agent‑friendly and addressed the current state of consumer AI. Chesky also argued that the world requires an AI‑native operating system to support these developments.
summary: Brian Chesky discussed making Airbnb more agent‑friendly. He also addressed the state of consumer AI and argued that the world needs an AI‑native operating system.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic asks Australian government for opt‑out model to train AI on local copyrighted works
content:
Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI system, has asked the Albanese government to grant “conditional approval” for big‑tech firms to train models on Australian copyrighted works using an opt‑out framework, after acknowledging it will not obtain a blanket copyright exemption. The company argues the technology could transform the economy.

Australia’s public broadcasters, the ABC and SBS, have criticised the proposal, warning that AI training on news content could “cannibalise” journalism. Both broadcasters are urging the government to introduce strict new media‑regulation rules that would require compensation for media organisations and protect public‑interest news.
summary: Anthropic has urged the Albanese government to consider granting conditional approval for big‑tech AI models to train on Australian copyrighted works using an opt‑out system, after conceding it will not secure a blanket copyright exemption. The ABC and SBS have strongly criticised the proposal and are calling for strict new rules to compensate media organisations and protect public‑interest journalism.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Experts warn AI could amplify election risks in south‑east Asia
content:
Some experts warn that artificial intelligence could be weaponised in South‑East Asia, a region characterised by predominantly young, hyper‑connected populations.  

In the past, large‑scale disinformation campaigns required extensive coordination, with teams of cyber operatives creating fake news websites, social‑media accounts and forged dossiers to spread false narratives.  

According to the experts, the advent of AI now allows similar disinformation efforts to be executed with far fewer resources, potentially amplifying election‑related risks across the region.
summary: Some experts fear AI could be weaponised in south‑east Asia, a region with predominantly young and hyper‑connected populations. They say that unlike past large‑scale cyber campaigns, AI now enables disinformation efforts with far less effort.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Over 44,000 file legal objections to Palantir‑run NHS Federated Data Platform
content:
More than 44,000 individuals have formally lodged legal objections to the use of their health data on the NHS‑run Federated Data Platform (FDP), which is powered by US‑based Palantir’s artificial‑intelligence technology. The campaign, which calls on NHS England to block the Palantir‑operated platform from handling personal information, reflects a broader backlash against the tech firm’s ties to the Israeli military and the Trump administration’s ICE enforcement actions. 

The objections allege that personal health records could be shared, stored, or used by the FDP without consent, prompting a coordinated effort to halt the system’s deployment across the national medical data network. The movement underscores growing public concern over data privacy and the involvement of private technology companies in public health infrastructure.
summary: Tens of thousands of people have formally demanded NHS England block the Palantir‑powered national medical data platform from handling their personal information. More than 44,000 have filed legal objections to their health data being shared, stored or used by the Federated Data Platform operated with the US company’s AI technology.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Dutch intelligence warns car tech could be used by hostile states to spy
content:
Dutch spy chiefs have warned that the technology embedded in modern cars can be used by hostile states to spy on drivers. According to the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD), cameras, microphones and GPS trackers in vehicles could be accessed by foreign actors.

The AIVD cautioned that these smart features could be exploited to eavesdrop on conversations, with microphones that can be switched on remotely. The warning comes amid concerns over Chinese imports of automotive technology.
summary: The Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) said microphones, cameras and GPS trackers in modern cars could be accessed by hostile states. It urged drivers to be aware of espionage risks, noting microphones can be switched on remotely to listen to conversations.
author: Guardian Technology

title: ChatGPT and Grok comply with prompt to erase hijabs from AI‑generated images
content:
The Guardian tested several AI chatbots after a French far‑right politician edited a photo to strip a Muslim woman of her hijab. The probe examined whether the bots would alter a similar image when asked.

The outlet prompted ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini and Claude to remove the veil from an AI‑generated picture of a woman wearing a hijab. Both OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok complied with the request, editing the image to eliminate the hijab.

Anthropic’s Claude replied that it lacks image‑editing or generation capabilities and stated it would not alter a photo to remove a hijab.
summary: The Guardian asked ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini and Claude to remove a hijab from an AI‑generated image of a Muslim woman. ChatGPT and Grok complied, while Claude said it lacks image‑editing features and would not alter the photo to remove the hijab.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Russia's jury reform criticized for shifting verdict power to judges
content:
Russia’s Supreme Court has proposed reforms to the country’s jury system that critics say shift verdict authority back to the state. The draft changes would let presiding judges “clarify” questions during jury deliberations and would cut the size of juries from six or eight members to four.

Lawyers argue that the measures undermine the independence of a system that historically acquits defendants at a rate 60 times higher than the national average in non‑jury trials. They contend that allowing judges to intervene in deliberations and reducing panel sizes could diminish the distinct role of juries in Russian courts.
summary: The Supreme Court proposals would let presiding judges "clarify" questions during deliberations and cut jury panels from six or eight members to four. Lawyers say the changes undermine the independence of a system that acquits at 60 times the national average in non‑jury trials.
author: Euronews

title: Videos show panic on FlyDubai flight after alleged cockpit attack, lands in Tabuk
content: Onboard videos captured by an Israeli passenger show panic aboard a FlyDubai flight after an alleged attack in the cockpit forced the aircraft to make an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The footage, released publicly, depicts chaotic scenes inside the cabin as passengers reacted to the incident. The emergency landing was prompted by the reported cockpit event, prompting authorities to intervene in Tabuk. No further details about injuries or the outcome of the investigation were provided.
summary: An Israeli passenger filmed
author: Euronews

title: Four sailors rescued after sperm whale sinks yacht in South Pacific
content:
Four sailors were rescued after a sperm whale struck and sank their yacht in the remote South Pacific.

A New Zealand Air Force surveillance aircraft coordinated the rescue, and the crew were taken aboard a cargo ship as their yacht went under.
summary: A sperm whale struck and sank a yacht in the remote South Pacific, leaving four sailors in need of rescue. A New Zealand Air Force surveillance aircraft coordinated the rescue and the crew were taken aboard a cargo ship as the yacht went under.
author: Euronews

title: Midday October 1, 2026 news bulletin highlights Europe and global stories
content:
On October 1, 2026, a midday news bulletin titled “Latest news bulletin” was released, inviting audiences to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond.

The bulletin highlights coverage of the latest news, breaking news, world affairs, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
summary: The midday bulletin on October 1, 2026 provides a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond. It covers latest and breaking news across world, business, entertainment, politics, culture, and travel.
author: Euronews

title: Bradley Whitford receives 2,858th Hollywood Walk of Fame star
content:
Bradley Whitford was presented with the 2,858th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. The ceremony took place in Los Angeles.

Whitford marked the occasion by celebrating with his family and fellow cast members from The West Wing after the star was unveiled.
summary: Bradley Whitford received the 2,858th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. He celebrated the honor with family and West Wing co‑stars in Los Angeles.
author: Euronews

title: Young students train in tai chi and kung fu on China's Wudang Mountains
content:
Young students from China and abroad are training in tai chi and kung fu on the historic Wudang Mountains, where ancient mountain schools preserve the art forms.  

The curriculum is guided by Taoist philosophy, which influences both the martial practices and the daily life of the participants.
summary: Young students from China and abroad are training in tai chi and kung fu on the Wudang Mountains. Taoist philosophy shapes the martial arts practice and daily life at the site.
author: Euronews

title: Russia orders expulsion of Hungarian embassy and consulate staff
content:
Moscow has ordered the staff of Hungary’s embassy and consulate to leave Russia, expelling the diplomats in a move that follows recent tensions between the two countries.  

The decision comes just weeks after Budapest expelled ten Russian diplomats in September, citing national‑security concerns. That expulsion was the first action of its kind by Hungary since Russia’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
summary: Moscow ordered Hungarian embassy and consulate staff to leave. This follows Budapest’s expulsion of 10 Russian diplomats in September on national security grounds, the first such move since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
author: Euronews

title: France's 2027 budget seeks 5.4 billion‑euro cuts to local government funding
content:
France presented its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, outlining a series of belt‑tightening measures that are expected to strain local services. The national government, which funds the majority of local and municipal budgets, is targeting 5.4 billion euros in savings from those budgets.

Mayors across the country are now scrambling to determine how to reduce expenditures while maintaining essential services, as the proposed cuts are described as painful for local governments. The budget plan therefore places significant pressure on municipalities to adjust their spending.
summary: France presented its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, proposing belt‑tightening measures that include 5.4 billion euros in savings for local and municipal budgets. Mayors across the country are scrambling to cut back while maintaining essential services.
author: France 24

title: France pushes 2027 budget belt‑tightening as bond investors grow wary
content:
France presented its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, outlining a set of unpopular belt‑tightening measures intended to reduce the deficit and calm increasingly nervous bond investors.  

The government hopes the fiscal tightening will appease investors ahead of next year’s presidential election.  

The proposal now faces a difficult passage through a deeply divided parliament, where political clans are positioning themselves for what is being described as one of the country’s most consequential elections in modern times.
summary: France presented its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, seeking unpopular belt‑tightening measures to lower the deficit and calm increasingly twitchy bond investors ahead of next year’s presidential election. The legislation faces a tough ride in a deeply divided parliament as political clans position themselves for the upcoming election.
author: France 24

title: Céline Dion uses AI and L‑Acoustics tech for quiet stage in France residency
content:
Céline Dion has launched a 16‑day residency in France as part of her comeback following years of illness. To maintain a quiet stage and preserve the clarity of her voice, her production team is employing both artificial intelligence and advanced sound‑system technology.

FRANCE24 journalist Peter O’Brien visited the venue after being invited by French audio firm L‑Acoustics, which provided the high‑tech equipment used for the performances.
summary: Céline Dion is performing a 16‑day residency in France after years of illness. Her team is using AI and high‑tech sound systems from L‑Acoustics, and FRANCE24's Peter O'Brien toured the setup at the company's invitation.
author: France 24

title: Hassan Hajjaj's 'Rock Stars' portraits of music icons debut at Paris Philharmonie
content:
Moroccan‑British artist and photographer Hassan Hajjaj is presenting a new exhibition of 40 vibrant “Rock Stars” portraits at the Philharmonie in Paris. The show features his colourful images of music and pop‑culture icons such as Madonna, Billie Eilish, Alicia Keys, Cardi B and Lee “Scratch” Perry.

Hajjaj explains that his instantly recognisable portraits are created by merging elements of his Moroccan heritage with the visual language of London street culture. He describes how the presence of a global superstar influences the dynamic of the shoot, shaping the final image in his signature style.
summary: Moroccan‑British artist and photographer Hassan Hajjaj has photographed major music and pop culture figures such as Madonna, Billie Eilish, Alicia Keys, Cardi B and Lee “Scratch” Perry. Forty of his vibrant “Rock Stars” portraits are now on display at the Philharmonie in Paris, where he explains his process of blending Moroccan heritage with London street culture.
author: France 24

title: 80% of Gaza infrastructure destroyed, 61 tonnes of rubble to clear, Google Maps shows
content:
New images posted this week by Google Maps depict the utter destruction across Gaza, where an estimated 80 percent of infrastructure has been destroyed.  

Analysts have calculated that about 61 tonnes of rubble must be cleared, a volume described as twenty times the total rubble generated by all wars worldwide over the past 18 years.
summary: New images posted this week by Google Maps show the utter destruction in Gaza. It’s been estimated that 61 tonnes of rubble need to be cleared, about 20 times the rubble generated in all wars worldwide over the last 18 years.
author: France 24

title: France holds Oct. 1 summit to boost New Caledonia nickel despite industry woes
content:
Paris is convening a summit on Thursday, October 1, to draw investors and boost wealth creation in France’s overseas territories. The French government will spotlight New Caledonia’s nickel sector as a key asset for potential investment.

Officials noted, however, that the nickel industry has been severely weakened by the political deadlock and tensions that have affected the archipelago in recent years.
summary: The French government is holding a summit on Thursday, October 1, to attract investors and revitalize wealth creation in France’s overseas territories. The event will highlight New Caledonian nickel, an industry that has been severely weakened by political deadlock and tensions in recent years.
author: France 24

title: Cameroon government announces payments amid indefinite university teachers strike
content:
The Cameroonian government announced it will make payments as an indefinite strike by university teachers continues.  

The strike was launched by SYNES, the National Union of Higher Education Teachers, and threatens the start of the academic year for universities, which had been scheduled for October 5.  

Teachers are demanding the payment of 16 billion CFA francs in academic bonuses, an amount equivalent to nearly 24 million euros.  

The ongoing strike could prevent the university term from beginning as planned.
summary: The start of the university academic year on Oct. 5 may be delayed because SYNES, the National Union of Higher Education Teachers, has launched an indefinite strike. Teachers are demanding the payment of 16 billion CFA francs in academic bonuses, and the government has announced payments as the strike continues.
author: France 24

title: UAE launches flydubai hijacking and terrorism investigation
content:
The UAE’s chief prosecutor has announced a new investigation into an alleged attempted hijacking of a flydubai commercial flight bound for Tel Aviv.  

The prosecutor said the investigation is looking at the possibility of “terrorist activity or intent” in the incident.  

It also confirmed that the UAE has jurisdiction over the case.
summary: The UAE's chief prosecutor said it is investigating possible terrorist activity or intent in the alleged attempted hijacking of a flydubai commercial flight to Tel Aviv. The prosecutor also stated that the UAE has jurisdiction over the case.
author: DW World

title: North and South Korea exchange accusations after landmine injures three soldiers
content:
North and South Korea have exchanged accusations over landmines after a mine blast injured three South Korean soldiers. The incident has intensified scrutiny of North Korea’s activities along the border.

The injuries to the three soldiers have prompted questions about North Korea’s strategic goals in the area. Both sides continue to blame each other for the presence of the mines.
summary: North and South Korea have exchanged accusations over a landmine that injured three South Korean soldiers. The blast has renewed scrutiny of North Korea's actions along the border and raised questions about its strategic goals.
author: DW World

title: Family of Renee Good sues Trump administration over fatal ICE shooting
content:
The family of Renee Good, a U.S. citizen who was fatally shot by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, has filed a lawsuit against President Donald Trump’s administration.  

Good was one of two U.S. citizens killed in the incident.  Her family claims the administration was negligent and violated her civil rights.
summary: The family of Renee Good, one of two U.S. citizens fatally shot by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, has filed a lawsuit. The suit alleges negligence and civil rights violations by President Donald Trump's administration.
author: DW World

title: Venezuelan Chavistas lament government's embrace of Trump
content:
Venezuelan supporters of Hugo Chávez have expressed disbelief at what they describe as an “utter surrealism” after the interim administration of Delcy Rodríguez signaled an embrace of U.S. President Donald Trump, according to reports.

Diehard Chavistas say the move represents an ideological U‑turn that contradicts the Bolivarian revolution’s leftist roots. Long‑time propagandist Mario Silva, a former host of the state‑funded television program The Razorblade, exemplifies the depth of devotion among Chávez loyalists; he regularly displayed Chávez’s portrait behind him and even tattooed the former president’s curly signature on his left wrist.
summary: Diehard Hugo Chávez supporters are struggling to comprehend the ideological U-turn being executed by Delcy Rodríguez’s interim administration. They lament the government's embrace of Trump.
author: Guardian World

title: UK PM Burnham says Iran likely behind RAF base incident
content:
UK Prime Minister Burnham has said that Iran is likely behind the recent incident at a Royal Air Force base. The statement was made in the context of growing concerns over Iranian involvement in the event.

UK, US and Israeli officials have also indicated that Iran was involved, but they have remained tight‑lipped on the specific details of the incident.
summary: UK Prime Minister Burnham said Iran is likely responsible for the incident at an RAF base. Officials from the UK, United States and Israel have also indicated Iranian involvement but have not disclosed further details.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ugandan asylum seeker in Japan creates samurai film amid deportation threat
content:
A Ugandan asylum seeker in Japan is turning to filmmaking as he faces possible deportation. The individual, identified as a filmmaker, is producing a samurai‑style movie that draws on his own life experiences.

The project, described as a samurai film, is being created while the asylum seeker confronts immigration proceedings that could lead to his removal from Japan.
summary: A Ugandan filmmaker facing deportation from Japan is turning to filmmaking. He is producing a samurai film that draws on his personal experiences.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Flydubai stabbing raises questions about cockpit security after 9/11 changes
content:
A stabbing aboard a Flydubai flight has prompted renewed questions about aircraft safety when a crew member becomes violent.  

Civil aviation security was overhauled after the September 2001 attacks to keep potential attackers out of cockpits. The Flydubai incident reverses that focus, highlighting the challenge of protecting passengers from aggression originating within the flight crew.
summary: Civil aviation changed after 9/11 to keep attackers outside cockpits. The Flydubai scare flips the dilemma.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Moroccan intelligence used spyware to silence journalists, Amnesty says
content:
Amnesty International says Moroccan intelligence services have employed surveillance tactics to “silence” journalists.  

A probe uncovered the use of spyware, hidden microphones and infected phones to monitor journalists, activists and rights defenders. The findings illustrate the breadth of monitoring carried out by the intelligence agencies.
summary: A probe found that Moroccan intelligence deployed spyware, hidden microphones and infected phones to surveil journalists, activists and rights defenders. Amnesty International says the surveillance was used to silence journalists.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Explosions heard in Addis Ababa after drone flights banned
content:
Explosions were reported in Ethiopia’s capital shortly after authorities prohibited drone flights in the city.  

The incident follows a week after fighting broke out north of the capital between the Ethiopian army and a newly formed alliance of armed groups.
summary: Explosions were heard in Ethiopia's capital. The incident comes a week after fighting erupted north of the capital between the army and a new alliance of armed groups.
author: BBC World

title: Trump’s AI rebrand to “super intelligence” spikes demand for .si Slovenian domains
content:
President Donald Trump has advocated renaming artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” abbreviated SI. The proposed label matches the two‑letter country code for Slovenia’s .si internet domains.

Following the president’s suggestion, demand for .si website names has surged, with observers describing the interest as unprecedented.
summary: President Trump wants AI renamed “super intelligence,” using the abbreviation SI. The change has caused unprecedented demand for Slovenian website names that share the SI initials.
author: BBC World

title: Brit Awards add £5m to Manchester economy, study says
content:
A recent study has found that hosting the Brit Awards in Manchester boosted the local economy by £5 million. The research highlights the financial impact of the event on the Greater Manchester region.

Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig welcomed the awards’ relocation north for the first time, describing it as a “massive moment.” Her remarks underscored the significance of the event for the city’s cultural and economic profile.
summary: A study found the Brit Awards boosted Manchester's economy by £5 million. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said the awards' move north for the first time was a “massive moment”.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: US filmmaker Hopwood DePree loses High Court case over Grade II-listed mansion
content:
US film‑maker Hopwood DePree has lost a High Court case over his attempt to acquire a Grade II‑listed mansion for £1.  

DePree had taken the council to court in a bid to take over the historic property at the nominal price.
summary: US filmmaker Hopwood DePree took the council to the High Court in a bid to acquire a Grade II‑listed mansion for £1. The court ruled against him, and he lost the case.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto no longer a protected witness in Portugal
content:
Rui Pinto, the 37-year-old whistleblower behind the website Football Leaks, will no longer be protected as a witness by Portuguese authorities. The decision to remove his protection was made on Wednesday, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Pinto’s leaks of private documents previously helped trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs.

Pinto has been a protected witness since 2020, a status he obtained after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest. He has now been advised to “exercise caution with family contacts” and to avoid social media.
summary: Work provided information concerning City’s financesHe called City decision ‘historic for English football’Rui Pinto, whose leaks of private documents helped to trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, will no longer be protected as a witness by the Portuguese authorities, it can be revealed. The removal of the whistleblower’s protection was decided on Wednesday, according to documents seen by the Guardian.

title: Rugby union power rankings: how the teams stand a year from World Cup
content:
South Africa remains the team to beat heading into the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia, following a decisive series victory over New Zealand. Although the Springboks were defeated by Australia in the most recent weekend, their comeback performance was emphatic, particularly after coach Rassie Erasmus emptied his bench. The team overcame an initial 1-0 deficit to secure a 3-1 series win, a result that underscores their status as the defending champions and primary contenders for the upcoming tournament.

The upcoming World Cup will feature 24 teams, with attention also turning to the hosts, Australia, as well as other major contenders like New Zealand, France, and England.
summary: There’s no ignoring the holders but what of the hosts, the All Blacks, France and even England? Here’s a rundown of all 24 teams taking part in Australia in 2027Beaten by Australia last weekend but the manner in which they came back after Rassie Erasmus emptied his bench was emphatic.

title: Money, family and sexism - why the number of women coaches is dropping
content: Despite recent on-pitch successes and increased media exposure for women's sport in the UK, major barriers continue to hinder progress in coaching. The decline in the number of women coaches is attributed to issues involving money, family responsibilities, and sexism.
summary: Despite recent on-pitch successes and increased media exposure for women's sport in the UK, major barriers remain - particularly in coaching.

title: Newcastle United coach Matthias Jaissle overcomes neck injury to play and coach
content:
Jaissle learned a lot about life after tumour aged five.

Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle could not move his neck at one point, but went on to play before embarking on a coaching career that sees him in Tyneside. He is currently the head coach of Newcastle United.
summary: Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle could not move his neck at one point. He later played before starting a coaching career in Tyneside.
author: BBC Sport

title: Slotkin criticizes Cornell handling of 2024 rape allegations
content:
Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) criticized her alma mater, Cornell University, for its handling of 2024 gang rape allegations against seven fraternity members. The university’s response to the incident has drawn national attention following a lawsuit filed earlier this month, which prompted several lawmakers to denounce the school.

The plaintiff, identified as Jane Doe, accused the men of the alleged assault. Slotkin, who earned her undergraduate degree at Cornell, stated that the institution has “lost its way” in its management of the case.
summary: Sen. Elissa Slotkin criticized Cornell University for its handling of 2024 gang rape allegations against seven fraternity members. A lawsuit filed by Jane Doe against the school brought the case into the national spotlight.
author: The Hill

title: Man Arrested for Verbal Threats Toward Texas State Capitol
content:
A man was arrested after making verbal threats toward the Texas State Capitol, according to a statement from Texas Governor Greg Abbott (R) on Wednesday evening.  

Governor Abbott confirmed the arrest and noted that the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) had intervened to stop a plot at the state’s capitol building in Austin. DPS told NBC Dallas‑Fort Worth that authorities had taken action to prevent the threat.
summary: A man was arrested after making verbal threats toward the Texas State Capitol, as confirmed by Governor Greg Abbott (R) on Wednesday evening. The Texas Department of Public Safety said authorities had stopped a plot at the state capitol building in Austin, according to NBC Dallas-Fort Worth.
author: The Hill

title: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike still alive after lethal injection, lawyers say
content:
Lawyers for Tennessee death‑row inmate Christa Pike claimed that she was still alive Wednesday night after receiving two syringes of lethal injection drugs.  

Pike’s federal public defenders filed a motion to the Tennessee Supreme Court noting that witnesses reported she had been given doses of pentobarbital at 8:26 p.m. But was “still alive and…”.
