title: Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as permanent Labor Secretary
content:
The United States Senate confirmed Keith Sonderling as the Secretary of Labor, voting 47‑41 on Wednesday night. Sonderling, who had been serving as the acting Secretary, was appointed to the position permanently, filling a vacancy in President Trump’s cabinet that had remained officially empty since April.

All Republicans present in the chamber voted in favor of Sonderling’s nomination, while all Democrats voted against it. The confirmation required only a simple majority, which the nomination achieved.

The vote marks the formal appointment of Sonderling to lead the Department of Labor.
summary: The Senate voted 47-41 to confirm Keith Sonderling, acting Secretary of Labor, as the permanent head of the Department of Labor. All Republicans present voted for the nomination and all Democrats voted against it.
author: The Hill

title: Becerra, Hilton clash over 'Trump' in California governor debate
content:
Former Health Secretary Xavier Becerra (D) and Republican Steve Hilton, a former Fox News host, clashed on the debate stage Wednesday as they jostled in a contentious race to replace California Governor Gavin Newsom (D).  

The rivals sparred over the economy, immigration and healthcare in an hour‑long CNN debate.  

The debate was the first and only scheduled.
summary: Former Health Secretary Xavier Becerra (D) and former Fox News host Steve Hilton (R) sparred over the economy, immigration and healthcare during an hourlong CNN debate. The debate was part of their race to replace California Gov. Gavin Newsom.
author: The Hill

title: Indiana Governor Mike Braun Extends Gas Tax Suspension, Adds Relief for Farmers
content:
Indiana Governor Mike Braun (R) announced on Wednesday that he is extending the state’s gas tax suspension. The extension comes as fuel prices rise amid the ongoing war in Iran.

Braun added that the new extension includes additional relief for farmers. In a post on the social platform X, he said, “Today I announced another gas tax extension with additional relief for farmers. Our farmers have the hardest job in America.”

The announcement reflects the governor’s response to the current fuel price surge.
summary: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun (R) announced on Wednesday that he is extending the state's gas tax suspension as fuel prices rise due to the ongoing war in Iran. The extension includes additional relief for farmers, according to a post on X.
author: The Hill

title: Study Finds More Rain Does Not Guarantee Higher River Flow
content:
Some rivers are getting more rain and snow, yet their water levels are falling, a new study shows. Researchers from Pennsylvania State University found that increased precipitation does not always translate into higher river flow, challenging the assumption that more rain means more water in rivers.

The study examined precipitation and river‑flow records from more than 10,000 rivers worldwide between 1951 and 2020. It found that in nearly one‑third of those rivers, flow trends diverged from the changes in rainfall and snow. The authors attribute this mismatch to global warming, which intensifies the hydrological cycle, making wet regions wetter and dry regions drier.

The findings suggest that climate change can alter river dynamics in ways that are not directly tied to local precipitation patterns.
summary: Researchers from Pennsylvania State University analyzed precipitation and river flow records in more than 10,000 rivers between 1951 and 2020. In nearly one-third of rivers, they found that flow trends did not match the changes observed in rainfall and snow.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Long‑acting medicines may eliminate daily tablets for some patients
content:
Long‑acting medicines could make daily tablets a thing of the past for some patients.  

For millions of people around the world, managing a long‑term health condition means remembering to take medicines every day, often for years. Advances in long‑acting medicines now allow some treatments to be taken only once a month, every few months, or even twice a year.
summary: Millions of people around the world manage long‑term health conditions by taking medicines every day for years. Advances in long‑acting medicines mean some treatments now need to be taken only once a month, every few months, or even twice a year.

title: COVID fatigue linked to reduced brain blood flow
content:
COVID fatigue linked to reduced brain blood flow

The article titled “COVID fatigue linked to reduced brain blood flow” notes that everyday activities such as playing with children or meeting a friend for coffee are often undertaken without consideration of the mental or physical energy required.
summary: Playing with your children or meeting a friend for coffee are everyday activities that many people move between without giving much thought to how much mental or physical energy they take. The article links COVID fatigue to reduced brain blood flow.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds climate change linked to skin disease changes in over 40% of nations
content:
A recent international study covering 136 countries found that more than 40 % of nations have reported climate‑related changes in the prevalence, severity, or both of skin disease. The research indicates that these shifts are linked to environmental changes associated with climate change.  

The study also highlights that lower‑income countries are disproportionately affected by these climate‑related changes in skin health.
summary: An international study of 136 countries found that more than 40% reported climate‑related changes in the prevalence, severity or both of skin disease. The impact was reported to be disproportionately greater in lower‑income countries.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Retatrutide yields substantial weight loss and better blood sugar in type 2 diabetes
content:
A new triple‑agonist therapy called retatrutide has been shown to produce substantial weight loss and improve blood‑sugar control in individuals who are obese or overweight and have type 2 diabetes. The findings will be presented at the Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan, Italy, scheduled for September 28 through October 2, and are published in The Lancet.

Researchers highlighted that this population typically achieves less weight loss from obesity medications than people without diabetes, making the observed results notable. The study underscores retatrutide’s potential as an effective treatment option for weight management and glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
summary: Research presented at the EASD Annual Meeting in Milan and published in The Lancet shows that the triple agonist therapy retatr
author: Medical Xpress

title: Wildlife tracking aims to fill gaps in monarch migration research
content:
A wildlife‑tracking effort is being launched to address long‑standing gaps in research on monarch butterfly migration.  

Each autumn, monarchs gather nectar from Iowa’s fall‑blooming wildflowers before beginning their extensive journey from North America to Mexico.  

The specific routes the butterflies follow and the ways weather and other factors influence their travel have largely remained unknown.  

The new tracking initiative is intended to illuminate those pathways and environmental impacts.
summary: Monarch butterflies feed on nectar from Iowa's fall‑blooming wildflowers each fall before migrating from North America to Mexico. Their migration pathways and how weather and other factors affect travel have largely remained a mystery.
author: Phys.org

title: Astronaut Kellie Gerardi posts pink flight jacket on Instagram, linking femininity and science
content:
Women astronauts are turning to social media to blend scientific credibility with expressions of femininity. In a recent Instagram post, astronaut, researcher and science communicator Kellie Gerardi shared a moment from a television interview in which she wore a bright pink flight jacket. The clip captured Gerardi’s six‑year‑old daughter asking, “Why can’t a flight jacket be pink or purple?” and then pointing at her mother on the screen with a delighted smile.

The post highlights Gerardi’s use of visual storytelling to challenge the notion that scientific professionalism must exclude traditionally feminine aesthetics. By pairing a bold, colored flight jacket with a credible media appearance, the exchange underscores a message that femininity and scientific authority can coexist.
summary: A six‑year‑old asked astronaut Kellie Gerardi why a flight jacket couldn’t be pink or purple, and Gerardi later appeared in a TV interview wearing a bright pink flight jacket. She posted the exchange on her Instagram account to show that femininity and scientific credibility are not mutually exclusive.
author: Phys.org

title: Swiss high‑altitude forests weakened by frequent droughts, increasing natural hazard risk
content:
Swiss high‑altitude forests are increasingly weakened by frequent summer droughts, a shift scientists attribute to global warming. The research indicates that the trees’ tolerance and resilience are being overwhelmed, pushing the forests to a tipping point.

Because these forests act as the primary barrier against avalanches, rockfalls, landslides and floods, their decline raises the danger of natural hazards for communities living in the valleys below.
summary: Scientists have shown that global warming has pushed Swiss forests to a tipping point where summer droughts exceed trees’ tolerance and resilience. The weakened forests reduce the first line of defense for valley communities against avalanches, rockfalls, landslides and floods.
author: Phys.org

title: Study links >90‑day spaceflights to higher astronaut hip fracture rates
content:
A study published in Mayo Clinic Proceedings reports that astronauts experience a higher rate of hip fractures after spaceflights lasting more than 90 days compared with those who undertake shorter missions or with individuals who are not astronauts.  

The research highlights the need for expanded assessment of astronauts’ long‑term skeletal health following extended periods in space.
summary: New research found that astronauts have higher rates of hip fractures after spaceflights lasting more than 90 days compared with shorter flights or non‑astronauts. The study published in Mayo Clinic Proceedings underscores the need for expanded assessment of astronauts' long‑term skeletal health.
author: Phys.org

title: Indonesian wildfire haze blankets Malaysia and Singapore, shuts schools
content:
Haze from Indonesian wildfires has blanketed neighboring Malaysia and Singapore for more than a month, prompting widespread health concerns.  

The prolonged smoke has forced school closures in both countries and sent respiratory complaints skyrocketing, while the affected nations face little legal recourse to address the transboundary pollution.
summary: Haze from Indonesian wildfires has blanketed Malaysia and Singapore for more than a month, closing schools. The pollution has driven respiratory complaints sharply upward, and there is little legal recourse.
author: Phys.org

title: Dutch farmer Sander Roeleveld harvests rice in Netherlands for first time
content:
Dutch farmers are testing rice as a new crop in an effort to address sinking peatlands, according to a recent report. The experiment is taking place in a soggy field situated between Amsterdam and The Hague.

title: Yantra LALR(1) parser generator for C++ builds full AST before walking
content:
Show HN: Yantra – an LALR(1) parser generator for C++  

Yantra, posted on Hacker News, is a C++ parser generator that produces a lexer, parser and abstract‑syntax‑tree (AST) walker from a single tool. Unlike most LALR parser generators such as Yacc, Bison or Lemon, which execute semantic actions during bottom‑up parsing, Yantra first builds the complete AST and then walks it top‑down in a separate pass. This design lets a parent rule’s action run before its children are visited and enables a single grammar to define multiple walkers—for example, one that emits C++ and another that emits Java—from the same parse.

The tool includes an integrated lexer with mode support (e.g., for nested comments) and offers an optional amalgamated single‑file output mode that generates a main() function. Yantra targets C++23, is released under the MIT license, and is currently at version 0.5.1 (pre‑1.0) with a single maintainer. Known gaps are listed at https://github. Com/TantrixAuto/yantra/blob/main/docs/known_l..., and the repository is hosted at https://github. Com/TantrixAuto/yantra. Feedback and questions are welcomed; the author will be monitoring comments.

The Hacker News post has earned 23 points and generated 14 comments.
summary: Yantra is a C++ parser generator that produces a lexer, parser, and AST walker from a single tool and constructs the entire AST before a separate top‑down walk. It includes an integrated lexer with mode support, optional single‑file output, C++23 compatibility, MIT licensing, and can generate multiple walkers such as C++ or Java emitters.

summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth launched a 120‑day study on the future of warfare. The study is led by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, and critics could point out that Musk's and Luckey's companies already sell the kinds of technology the study is likely to recommend.
author: TechCrunch

title: Gov. Gavin Newsom signs California laws banning AI worker surveillance and firing
content:
Governor Gavin Newsom signed legislation on Wednesday aimed at shielding California workers from the perceived threats of artificial intelligence, including job losses and workplace surveillance.  

The new laws prohibit employers from using AI to predict a worker’s emotional state through biometric data, require written notices to employees when AI is responsible for mass layoffs, and bar the use of AI in decisions to terminate employment.  

Newsom, a Democrat, also criticized former President Donald Trump for not advancing comprehensive federal AI regulations.
summary: Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws on Wednesday to protect California workers from AI threats such as job loss and workplace surveillance. The measures prohibit employers from using biometric data to predict emotional states, require written notice for AI-driven mass layoffs, and ban AI from deciding terminations.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI tools to advise farmers on harvest timing
content:
A discussion is emerging about the role of artificial intelligence in agriculture, specifically whether AI tools could assist farmers in deciding when to harvest fruit. The question centers on whether growers will adopt such technology to guide harvest timing.

The alternative under consideration is whether farmers will continue to rely on their own intuition to make those decisions, rather than incorporating AI-based recommendations.
summary: Farmers may consider AI tools to help judge when to pick fruit. The decision is whether to use technology or rely on intuition.
author: BBC Technology

title: Flydubai Flight FZ 1073 Plunges Near Jordan, Passengers Compare to Rollercoaster
content:
A flydubai aircraft on flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv plunged dramatically as it neared the Jordanian border on Wednesday. Passengers reported that the plane entered a rapid dive, losing thousands of feet in seconds.

Almog Italie, a passenger on the flight, told AFP the experience felt like “very big turbulence, but there was no turbulence,” likening the sudden loss of altitude to riding a “rollercoaster.” The incident was reported by France 24’s August Hakansson.
summary: Passengers on flydubai flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv reported the aircraft began a rapid dive near the Jordanian border on Wednesday. Almog Italie told AFP that the sudden loss of thousands of feet of altitude felt like riding a rollercoaster, with no turbulence present.
author: France 24

title: Federal judge approves settlement clearing Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery
content:
A federal judge approved a settlement on Wednesday, clearing Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery after 12 U.S. states challenged the deal on antitrust grounds.

The agreement contains safeguards for CNN’s editorial independence and requires the merged studio to release at least 30 films a year for its first two years.

With the settlement approved, the deal now clears the legal hurdle.
summary: A federal judge approved a settlement clearing Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery after 12 US states challenged the deal on antitrust grounds. The agreement includes safeguards for CNN’s editorial independence and requires the merged studio to release at least 30 films a year for its first two years.
author: France 24

title: Trump urges former Fed chief Powell to resign after watchdog report
content:
The Federal Reserve’s internal watchdog reported Wednesday that it found no basis for a criminal referral concerning a roughly $1 billion cost overrun on renovations to the central bank’s Washington buildings, though it criticized the project’s oversight.

The report’s conclusions prompted President Donald Trump to renew his call for former Federal Reserve chief Jerome Powell to resign.
summary: Federal Reserve watchdog found no grounds for a criminal referral over a roughly $1 billion cost overrun on renovations to the central bank's Washington buildings, but faulted project oversight. The findings prompted President Donald Trump to renew his call for former Fed chief Jerome Powell to resign.
author: France 24

title: UN debate centers on who shapes AI, power, trust and inclusion
content:
The United Nations is holding a debate on who will shape the future of artificial intelligence (AI) and who will reap its benefits.  

Artificial Intelligence, or AI, and the technology that powers it is advancing rapidly.  

The central question being raised worldwide is who gets a seat at the table deciding how AI is used and who ultimately benefits from its deployment.
summary: Artificial Intelligence is advancing rapidly. The global debate centers on who gets a seat at the table to decide its use and who benefits.
author: UN News

title: US judge approves settlement for Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros
content:
A U.S. judge has approved a settlement that clears the way for Paramount to acquire Warner Bros., ending legal obstacles to the transaction.

The deal, described as mammoth, has prompted scrutiny over the potential impact of such a large media consolidation. Critics have voiced concerns that the merger could affect editorial independence across the industry.

The approval allows the acquisition to move forward while the broader debate over corporate concentration in media continues.
summary: A US judge approved a settlement that allows Paramount to acquire Warner Bros. The mammoth deal has raised questions about corporate consolidation and editorial independence in media.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump says an Israeli plumber helped land Flydubai flight
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said he was amazed by a recent anecdote he shared about an “Israeli plumber.”  

Trump recounted that the plumber played a role in landing a Flydubai flight, highlighting the unexpected involvement of the individual in the aircraft’s safe arrival.
summary: US President Donald Trump said he was amazed by a story about an Israeli plumber. He said the plumber helped land a Flydubai flight.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump says US could “blow up” Iran or strike a deal, warns standoff ending soon
content: Former President Donald Trump hinted that the United States could “blow up” Iran or reach a deal, saying the current standoff would end very soon one way or the other. Trump made the remarks while discussing the escalating tensions between the two nations. He warned that the time for resolution was approaching, though he did not specify a timeline or the conditions that would lead to either outcome.
summary: Trump said the United States may “blow up” Iran or strike a deal. He insisted the standoff will end very soon one way or the other.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli passengers describe nightmare on Flydubai flight diverted after pilot stabbed
content:
Israeli passengers described a “nightmare” experience aboard a Flydubai flight that was diverted after a pilot was stabbed. The travelers recounted the horror they faced during the incident.

The flight’s diversion was prompted by the stabbing of the pilot, prompting the airline to change course while passengers endured the unsettling situation.
summary: Israeli passengers described the onboard experience as a nightmare. The flight was diverted after a pilot was stabbed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: California bans child marriage, Gov. Gavin Newsom calls it overdue protection
content: California has enacted a ban on child marriage, ending the practice within the state. The new law arrives while child marriage remains legal in 32 other U.S. states. Governor Gavin Newsom called the measure a “long overdue measure to protect young Californians.”
summary: California has enacted a ban on child marriage. Governor Gavin Newsom said the measure is a long overdue step to protect young Californians.
author: BBC World

title: Dr Ning Xu denies rule breach in Nikon Small World In Motion contest
content:
A tiny image entered in Nikon’s annual Small World In Motion contest has provoked a strong backlash among participants and observers.  

Dr. Ning Xu has responded to the criticism, stating that he did not break any of the contest’s rules.  

The dispute centers on the image’s size and the allegations of rule violations, which Dr. Xu continues to reject.
summary: Dr Ning Xu says he did not violate the rules of Nikon's Small World In Motion contest. The contest is Nikon's annual Small World In Motion competition.
author: BBC World

title: Swiss glaciers suffer disastrous ice loss, threatening water supplies
content:
Swiss glaciers have endured a “disastrous” year of ice loss, prompting concerns that the reduction could jeopardise water supplies.  

Scientists say the rapid melting is no longer surprising given the pace of climate change.  

The extent of the ice loss underscores growing worries about the future availability of water sourced from the Alpine region.
summary: Swiss glaciers experienced a disastrous year of ice loss that threatens water supplies. Scientists say the rapid melting is no longer surprising given the pace of climate change.
author: BBC World

title: US Supreme Court permits Christa Pike execution to proceed
content:
The U.S. Supreme Court has permitted the execution of Christa Pike to proceed.  

The lethal‑injection death was originally set for earlier on Wednesday, but a lower court intervened and paused the execution.  

With the Supreme Court’s authorization, the execution is now slated to move forward.
summary: The US Supreme Court allowed the execution of Christa Pike to go ahead. The lethal injection had been scheduled for earlier on Wednesday before a lower court paused the execution.
author: BBC World

title: Putin shows no sign of ending war as Russia intensifies Ukraine invasion
content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to deliver a foreign‑policy speech that analysts say will be closely watched. The title of the address underscores that, despite international pressure, Russia appears to be maintaining its military campaign in Ukraine.

All available indications point to the full‑scale invasion continuing, suggesting that Moscow is not showing any sign of ending the war or scaling back its operations.
summary: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched. All signs point to the full‑scale invasion continuing.
author: BBC World

title: Crew-13 astronauts set for six-month launch to ISS after delays
content:
Crew-13 astronauts are set to launch to the International Space Station following several weeks of delays. The mission team consists of one veteran astronaut and three first-time flyers who are preparing to begin their assignment.

The crew is scheduled to embark on a six-month mission aboard the space station.
summary: One veteran astronaut and three first-time flyers are ready to begin a six-month mission to the ISS. The crew is preparing for launch after experiencing weeks of delays.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Sussexes condemn reckless intrusion after photographer spotted near Archie and Lilibet's school
content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have condemned what they described as "reckless intrusion" after a photographer was spotted near the school attended by their children, Archie and Lilibet. The incident occurred outside a UK school where the two children are enrolled.

One of the two men observed at the location is understood to be an international press photographer. The royal couple's statement highlights their concern over the privacy of their family in the vicinity of the children's educational institution.
summary: The Sussexes have condemned what they describe as reckless intrusion following a sighting near their children's school. One of two men seen outside the school is understood to be an international press photographer.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Dame Esther Rantzen, That's Life! presenter and Childline founder, dies
content:
Dame Esther Rantzen, a prominent television presenter and campaigner, is known for her two-decade tenure hosting the program That's Life!. Beyond her television career, she established two national helplines, one of which was Childline.

Rantzen also became a notable advocate for assisted dying, using her public profile to champion the cause.
summary: Dame Esther Rantzen presented the show That's Life! for two decades. She also set up two national helplines, including Childline.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Veteran broadcaster Dame Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
content:
Veteran broadcaster Dame Esther Rantzen has died at the age of 86. She is best known for fronting the BBC program That's Life for two decades.

Beyond her television career, Rantzen went on to found the charity Childline. In recent years, she was also active as a campaigner for assisted dying.
summary: Dame Esther Rantzen, who fronted the BBC's That's Life for two decades, has died at the age of 86. She also founded Childline and was a campaigner for assisted dying in recent years.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Shubman Gill hits fastest ODI double century as India chase 406
content:
India captain Shubman Gill scored an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls to lead his team to an eight-wicket victory against West Indies in Guwahati on Wednesday. This performance secured the second-highest successful chase in one-day international history, as India chased down a target of 406.

Gill’s innings marked the fastest double century in ODI history, achieved in just 117 balls, while also setting the record for the quickest ODI century of his career at 62 balls. The 27-year-old, the world’s top-ranked ODI batter, became only the second player after Rohit Sharma to score multiple double centuries in the format.

The match followed a high-scoring first innings by West Indies, who posted 405 after hitting three centuries.
summary: Shubman Gill remained unbeaten on 223 off 133 balls to record the fastest double century in one-day international history. India secured an eight-wicket victory against West Indies to complete the format's second-highest successful chase.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tuchel identifies Bellingham as England No 9 alternative to Kane
content:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel has identified Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham as a potential alternative to Harry Kane in the No 9 position. This assessment comes as Tuchel searches for depth in the attack, noting that Kane currently has little cover up front.

Harry Kane continued his scoring record during England’s 2-0 Nations League victory against Czechia in Prague on Tuesday. The late strike moved Kane to 87 goals in 123 international appearances. While Tuchel expressed confidence that the 33-year-old striker can last another decade at the highest level and reach a century of international goals soon, he acknowledged that England cannot expect to produce a replica of their greatest forward.
summary: England head coach Thomas Tuchel has identified Jude Bellingham as a potential option to play at No 9 for the national team. Kane scored his 87th international goal in a 2-0 win against Czechia, but Tuchel noted concerns over England's lack of depth in attack.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Anthony Joshua says he is in contact with Peter Fury ahead of December cardiff fight
content:
Anthony Joshua has revealed he is in contact with Peter Fury, the uncle and former trainer of Tyson Fury, marking a surprising development in the buildup to their heavyweight bout scheduled for December in Cardiff. The two former world champions are set to face each other after a period of intense pre-fight promotion, with Joshua’s statement highlighting an unexpected connection between the camps.

The relationship between Peter Fury and Tyson Fury has been strained for years following their split over an apparent financial dispute. Peter Fury had previously trained Tyson when he defeated Wladimir Klitschko to claim his first world heavyweight title in 2015. Despite the long-standing silence between the uncle and nephew, Joshua’s disclosure suggests a new dynamic in the lead-up to their upcoming match.

At a recent London press conference, Tyson Fury vowed to “blast him out,” maintaining the aggressive tone typical of the rivalry. The combination of personal feuds, professional history, and direct threats continues to define the narrative surrounding the December fight in Cardiff.
summary: Anthony Joshua revealed he is in contact with Tyson Fury's uncle Peter Fury, a surprising development in the buildup to their December fight in Cardiff. The two former world champions met at a London press conference where Fury vowed to "blast him out."
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rivals say relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enough
content:
Premier League executives from rival clubs are calling for a severe sanction that would force Manchester City into a prolonged absence from the top flight, arguing that a single-season relegation to the Championship is insufficient. This pressure follows the club’s guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of financial rule-breaking.

An independent commission described the violations as a “disguised funding scheme” and “sham commercial deals” that allowed Manchester City to artificially inflate their income by £900m between 2009 and 2018. Manchester City maintains that they are “innocent of the accusations.”
summary: Premier League executives stated that a one-season relegation would be insufficient punishment after Manchester City was found guilty of over 100 financial rule-breaking charges. The club maintained they are innocent of the accusations, which involved a disguised funding scheme that artificially inflated income by £900 million between 2009 and 2018.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pep Guardiola speaks in Wembley press room after Manchester City’s 6-0 Watford win in May 2019
content:
Pep Guardiola reflected on the nature of Manchester City and football in a recent statement. He asked, “Do you know the question that you are asking me? Today, do you honestly think it is my job to make this kind of question happen …,” before pausing for a long, painful moment.

The comments were made in the Wembley press room an hour after Manchester City’s 6‑0 defeat of Watford in May 2019. Guardiola described a shift from cheerfully toasting his own FA Cup final victory to “a grizzled chief detective addressing a room full of convicted perverts.”

He added that success “drowns out every other noise in football” and that history is written by domestic treble winners, a truth that can change “right up until the moment it isn’t.”
summary: Guardiola was in the Wembley press room an hour after Manchester City defeated Watford 6-0 in May 2019. The commentary describes his demeanor shifting from celebrating an FA Cup final victory to a more critical, investigative tone.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Arsenal Draw 2-2 with Paris FC After Misa Rodriguez and Leah Williamson Miscommunication
content:
Arsenal dropped points in the Women's Champions League after allowing a two-goal lead to slip, resulting in a 2-2 draw with Paris FC. The match concluded in a stalemate following a late equalizer for the visiting team.

The equalizing goal stemmed from a miscommunication between Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez and England captain Leah Williamson. This defensive error gifted Paris FC the opportunity to level the score in the final moments of the game.
summary: Arsenal conceded a late equalizer to Paris FC after a miscommunication between goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez and Leah Williamson. The match ended in a 2-2 draw in the Women's Champions League.
author: BBC Sport

title: Fury and Joshua trade jokes and pleasantries at London news conference
content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua held a news conference in London, marking a shift in their dynamic after more than a decade of public feuding and false starts. The two boxers exchanged pleasantries and traded jokes during the event.

The atmosphere was characterized by mutual respect and humor, with the fighters even discussing the possibility of going for a pint together.
summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua exchanged pleasantries and jokes at a news conference in London. The event marked a shift after more than a decade of public feuding and false starts between the two boxers.
author: BBC Sport

title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp after coach denies rift
content: Cristiano Ronaldo has departed Portugal’s international camp, stating that he will provide an explanation for his departure "in time." This move occurred hours after head coach Jorge Jesus publicly denied the existence of any rift between himself and the player.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo stated he has left Portugal's international camp and will explain his reasons in time. This decision came hours after head coach Jorge Jesus denied any rift with the player.
author: BBC Sport

title: Sen. Rand Paul blocks unanimous consent push for Kids Online Safety Act
content:
Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) blocked a Wednesday effort by Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) and Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) to pass the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA) by unanimous consent. The legislation is a long-sought bill designed to protect children in the digital space.

KOSA aims to hold social media companies accountable for alleged harms.
summary: Sen. Rand Paul blocked an effort by Sens. Richard Blumenthal and Marsha Blackburn to pass the Kids Online Safety Act by unanimous consent. The bill aims to protect children in the digital space and hold social media companies accountable for alleged harms.
author: The Hill

title: Trump: South Korea to invest up to $200B in Alaska LNG, US power plants
content:
President Trump announced on Wednesday that the South Korean government will invest up to $200 billion in U.S. energy infrastructure. The announcement was made during remarks in the Oval Office.

The investment portfolio includes a natural gas pipeline in Alaska, a natural gas plant in Texas, and eight new nuclear power plants across the country.
summary: President Trump announced that the South Korean government will invest up to $200 billion in U.S. energy infrastructure. The investment includes a natural gas pipeline in Alaska, a natural gas plant in Texas, and eight new nuclear power plants.
author: The Hill

title: Trump asks Attorney General Todd Blanche to study report clearing Powell
content:
President Trump stated on Wednesday that he has directed U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche to “study” a report from the Office of Inspector General. The report cleared former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell of criminal wrongdoing concerning renovations at the central bank.

Trump wrote that he asked Blanche to examine the document and make a determination regarding the matter.
summary: President Trump wrote that he asked U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche to study the Office of Inspector General’s report that cleared former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell of criminal wrongdoing related to the central bank’s renovations. He also requested Blanche to make a determination based on that report.
author: The Hill

title: Senate Democrats block data center bill
content:
Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act, a bill aimed at addressing data center electricity costs, by failing to provide the 60 votes necessary for passage. The Democratic opposition characterized the legislation as ineffective and “toothless.”

The bill had previously passed the House of Representatives with significant bipartisan support before facing obstruction in the Senate.
summary: Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act, which seeks to address data center electricity costs. They described the legislation as ineffective and "toothless," despite it passing the House with significant bipartisan support.
author: The Hill

title: American Oversight sues DHS over missing records on 250,000 noncitizen voter registrations
content: American Oversight filed a lawsuit against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on Wednesday after the agency failed to provide records supporting Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s claim that 250,000 non-U.S. citizens registered to vote across four states. The watchdog group initiated the legal action following its Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests for relevant documents.
summary: The watchdog group American Oversight sued the Department of Homeland Security after the agency failed to provide records supporting Secretary Markwayne Mullin's claim. The lawsuit follows the group's Freedom of Information Act requests for data on 250,000 non-U.S. citizens registered to vote in four states.
author: The Hill

title: Trump defends government-funded ads, says not promoting candidate
content:
President Trump defended government-funded ad campaigns on Wednesday, stating that he is not promoting a specific candidate. He told reporters, “I’m not running for office first of all,” and characterized his messaging as a “countrywide ad” focused on the “spirit of our country” rather than a particular political figure.

In his defense, Trump emphasized that discussions about “making America great” and “making our country great” serve as advertisements for the nation as a whole.
summary: President Trump defended his government-funded ad campaigns by stating he is not promoting a particular candidate. He described the ads as countrywide messages focused on making the country great.
author: The Hill

title: Pennsylvania records fifth measles-related death amid worst outbreak in 35 years
content:
Pennsylvania health officials reported a fifth measles-associated death on Wednesday, marking the latest casualty in an outbreak that has become the worst the commonwealth has experienced in over 35 years. The Pennsylvania health department identified the deceased as an unvaccinated resident of Lancaster County, though no further details about the individual were released.

In a statement accompanying the announcement, officials noted the severity of the situation as the number of cases continues to rise across the state.
summary: Pennsylvania health officials reported a fifth measles-associated death on Wednesday, noting the victim was an unvaccinated resident of Lancaster County. The state is currently experiencing its worst measles outbreak in over 35 years.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Highlights Sen. Sullivan in $54B Alaska Gas Export Announcement
content:
President Trump announced a $54 billion investment in a project to export natural gas from Alaska on Wednesday, placing Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska) at the center of the event. The announcement highlighted Sullivan’s role in the initiative as the president unveiled the details of the infrastructure plan.

The Alaska natural gas export project is part of a broader $200 billion investment from South Korea into the United States. This multi-billion dollar package includes the liquefied natural gas project, eight nuclear power plants, and a 6-gigawatt facility, though the full scope of the latter was not specified in the available information.
summary: President Trump announced a $54 billion investment in an Alaska natural gas export project, placing Sen. Dan Sullivan at the center of the reveal. The project is part of a broader $200 billion South Korean investment in the U.S. that includes nuclear power plants.
author: The Hill

title: Two charged in scheme to import counterfeit Ozempic from China to U.S. distributors
content:
Federal prosecutors have charged two people in an alleged scheme to bring counterfeit versions of the type‑2 diabetes drug Ozempic from China and sell them to U.S. distributors.  

The charges allege that the defendants planned to import the fake medication and distribute it within the United States.  

Federal prosecutors have charged two individuals in this alleged scheme.
summary: Federal prosecutors have charged two people in an alleged scheme to bring fake versions of the type 2 diabetes drug Ozempic from China. The defendants allegedly planned to sell the counterfeit medication to U.S. distributors.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Combo therapy targets genetic vulnerability in clear cell renal cancer
content: Researchers have identified a genetic vulnerability in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, the most aggressive form of kidney cancer, that could be exploited by a combination treatment strategy. The approach aims to trigger the cancer cells to self‑destruct, according to a study recently published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
summary: Researchers found a genetic vulnerability in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, the most aggressive type of kidney cancer. The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, suggests a combination treatment could cause the cancer cells to self‑destruct.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Trevogrumab reduces lean mass loss by 50% during semaglutide treatment
content:
New research presented at the annual meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan, Italy, from September 28 to October 2, indicates that trevogrumab can help preserve lean mass during semaglutide-induced weight loss. The study, which is also in press at The Lancet, demonstrates that trevogrumab reduces lean mass loss by 50% compared to semaglutide combined with placebo.

Trevogrumab functions by inhibiting a protein that negatively regulates muscle mass. The findings were shared during the EASD annual meeting, highlighting the potential of this anti-myostatin therapy to mitigate muscle loss associated with semaglutide treatment.
summary: New research presented at the EASD meeting shows that trevogrumab can reduce lean mass loss during semaglutide treatment by 50% compared with semaglutide and placebo. The study, also in press at The Lancet, indicates that the anti-myostatin drug helps preserve lean mass during and after weight loss.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds nail detachment over 4x more common in GLP-1 users
content: Nail detachment is more than four times as common among individuals taking GLP-1 receptor agonists compared to comparable people with obesity or type 2 diabetes who are not taking the drugs. This finding comes from the first controlled study to examine the potential effects of these medications on nail health.
summary: The first controlled study indicates that nail detachment is more than four times as common among people taking GLP-1 receptor agonists. This increased frequency was observed compared to comparable individuals with obesity or type 2 diabetes who are not taking the drugs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Ofglipron pill matches insulin safety for diabetes patients at cardiovascular risk
content:
New research presented at the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) annual meeting in Milan, Italy, indicates that a daily orforglipron pill offers a potential alternative to insulin injections for type 2 diabetes patients at increased cardiovascular risk. The study, published in The Lancet, found that orforglipron provided cardiovascular safety comparable to daily insulin glargine injections while achieving greater improvements in weight and blood sugar control.

Despite these benefits, the research noted that gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent among patients taking orforglipron, which resulted in a higher rate of treatment discontinuations. The study was sponsored by Eli Lilly, the manufacturer of orforglipron.
summary: Research presented at the EASD annual meeting found that the daily orforglipron pill offered cardiovascular safety comparable to insulin glargine injections while improving weight and blood sugar control. However, gastrointestinal adverse events were more common with orforglipron, leading to more treatment discontinuations.
author: Medical Xpress

title: MGM CEO Leaves Door Open to People Inc. Bid Amid Casino M&A Activity
content:
MGM CEO has left the door open to a potential bid from People Inc. as casino dealmaking activity intensifies. The Wall Street Journal reported that MGM is currently exploring an offer for People Inc., a move that follows a recent shift in the companies' relationship.

Previously, People Inc. had proposed to buy the remainder of MGM at a price of $48.30 per share. However, People Inc. subsequently withdrew that acquisition proposal, leading to the current exploration of a reverse offer by MGM.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that MGM is exploring an offer for People Inc. This development follows People Inc. withdrawing its $48.30-per-share proposal to acquire the remainder of MGM.
author: CNBC Business

title: Fed watchdog finds no criminal violations in $2.4bn renovation cost overruns
content:
An internal Federal Reserve watchdog reported that the central bank mismanaged costs for a $2.4 billion renovation of its Washington DC headquarters, though the investigation found no criminal violations. The report was released on Wednesday, concluding a period of scrutiny that included a months-long Department of Justice criminal investigation which was dropped in April.

President Donald Trump has spent over a year criticizing the renovation project, using it as a focal point for attacks against the Federal Reserve and former chair Jerome Powell. These criticisms occurred amid broader efforts to pressure Powell into lowering interest rates.
summary: An internal watchdog report found that the Federal Reserve mismanaged costs for a $2.4bn renovation of its Washington DC headquarters but noted no criminal violations occurred. Donald Trump had criticized the project and pressured former Fed chair Jerome Powell, leading to a Department of Justice criminal investigation that was dropped in April.
author: Guardian Business

title: Fin and sperm whales shift distribution rapidly in Mediterranean
content:
Researchers are investigating the distribution of large marine animals in the Mediterranean, including fin whales, sperm whales, and bottlenose dolphins. Evidence indicates that these species shift between marine areas over remarkably short timeframes and relatively small spatial scales.

While some species, such as the striped dolphin, maintain a relatively stable presence in specific areas, others like the fin whale exhibit significant movement. Fin whales, for instance, concentrate in different areas from one observation campaign to the next, highlighting the dynamic nature of their distribution.
summary: Research indicates that Mediterranean marine species like fin and sperm whales shift between areas in short timeframes and over small spatial scales. In contrast, striped dolphins maintain a relatively stable presence in certain areas.
author: Phys.org

title: CU Boulder study links time perception, not quantity, to mental health
content:
A new study from the University of Colorado Boulder suggests that feeling short on time may have positive implications for mental health. The research indicates that the subjective perception of one's available time is more significant for mental well-being than the actual amount of time possessed.

The study examines the relationship between time and mental health, highlighting that how individuals feel about their time is a key factor in their psychological state.
summary: A new University of Colorado Boulder study examines the relationship between time and mental health. The research suggests that how individuals feel about their available time is more significant than the actual amount of time they have.
author: Phys.org

title: Chalmers AI scientist autonomously generates and validates new biological discoveries
content:
Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden have developed an AI scientist that can generate scientific hypotheses, design experiments, and interpret results. This system is capable of making new biological discoveries with minimal human intervention.

The development represents an important advance in the field of self-driving laboratories.
summary: Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology developed an AI scientist that generates hypotheses, designs experiments, and interprets results. This system makes new biological discoveries with minimal human intervention, representing an important advance in self-driving laboratories.
author: Phys.org

title: Border entry reveals gap in international human rights law, new analysis argues
content:
A new analysis published in the International Journal of Migration and Border Studies argues that international human rights law contains a significant gap regarding border entry. The study contends that while the legal framework protects migrants once they are within a state's jurisdiction, it does not recognize a right to enter another country.

The authors of the analysis maintain that this limitation renders the current system incomplete.
summary: International human rights law protects migrants once they are within a state's jurisdiction but stops short of recognizing the right to enter another country, according to a new analysis in the International Journal of Migration…
author: Phys.org

title: Tibet Ice Cores Reveal Last Ice Age Fragments, Extending Glacial Record
content:
Ice cores recovered from an ice cap in northwestern Tibet appear to preserve fragments of ancient ice from the last ice age. According to a new study, these findings extend Earth's glacial record by more than 100,000 years.

The recovered samples are the oldest ice cores ever obtained from the region, providing new insights into high-altitude glacial history.
summary: Ice cores from a northwestern Tibet ice cap preserve ancient fragments from the last ice age. These cores extend the region's glacial record by more than 100,000 years, making them the oldest ever recovered there.
author: Phys.org

title: Fluorescent sensors could help researchers see diabetes in action
content: Researchers from the University of Bath have developed fluorescent molecular probes capable of detecting changes in glucose levels inside living animals. These tools provide scientists with new methods to visualize sugar uptake and study metabolic diseases, including diabetes and cancer, in whole organisms in real time. The findings from this research have been published in the journal Advanced Science.
summary: Researchers from the University of Bath have developed fluorescent molecular probes that can detect changes in glucose levels inside living animals, giving scientists new ways of visualizing sugar uptake and studying diabetes, cancer and other metabolic diseases in whole organisms in real time. The findings are published in the journal Advanced Science.
author: Phys.org

title: UC Santa Cruz scientists develop chemical cue method to predict toxic algal blooms
content: A team of marine scientists led by researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz, has developed a new approach for predicting harmful algal blooms (HABs). This method utilizes chemical cues from ocean predators to provide early warnings of these hazardous marine events. The development marks a shift in how oceanographers track and anticipate such occurrences.
summary: A team of marine scientists led by researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz, has developed a new approach to predicting harmful algal blooms. This method changes how oceanographers track these hazardous marine events.
author: Phys.org

title: NASA, International Partners Advance Work on Space Crops
content: NASA, the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), and the German Aerospace Center have signed a joint statement of intent to initiate coordinated preparatory work. The agreement focuses on developing an Earth-based demonstrator designed to determine how to grow crops on the Moon.
summary: NASA, CSA (Canadian Space Agency), and the German Aerospace Center signed a joint statement of intent to begin coordinated, preparatory work toward an Earth-based demonstrator to learn how to grow crops on the Moon.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Awards Modulate Space Contract for Lunar 5G with Wi-Fi 6
content:
NASA has awarded Modulate Space Corporation a contract to develop key elements of a 5G communications system for the lunar surface. The system, which includes built-in Wi-Fi 6, is being developed for NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland.

The accelerated effort is organized into two primary work areas aimed at creating a scalable, standards-based communications capability.
summary: NASA has awarded Modulate Space Corporation a contract to develop a 5G communications system with built-in Wi-Fi 6 for the lunar surface. The project is organized into two primary work areas to create a scalable, standards-based communications capability for NASA’s Glenn Research Center.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Selects Three New Moon Science Investigations for Future Lunar Base
content: NASA has selected three new scientific investigations and their associated payload suites to enhance understanding of the Moon and support the development of Moon Base, humanity’s first lunar outpost. These instruments and technologies were chosen through the Payloads and Research Investigations on the Surface of the Moon (PRISM) program.
summary: NASA selected three new scientific investigations and their payload suites to advance knowledge of the Moon and support the development of humanity’s first lunar outpost, Moon Base. The instruments and technologies were chosen through NASA’s Payloads and Research Investigations on the Surface of the Moon (PRISM) program.
author: NASA News

title: Overlapping Galaxies Reveal Cosmic Dust
content:
A collection of overlapping galaxies is being used to study cosmic dust, according to a new astronomical effort described as an “overlap zoo.”  

Galaxies are vast assemblies of billions of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity and scattered across the immensity of space. Occasionally, from Earth’s perspective or that of a space telescope, two galaxies line up and appear to overlap in the sky.  

These rare overlapping configurations provide a natural laboratory for researchers to examine the distribution and characteristics of interstellar dust. By observing how the foreground galaxy’s dust dims and reddens the light from the background galaxy, astronomers can gain insight into the composition and amount of cosmic dust present.
summary: Two galaxies sometimes line up from Earth’s perspective, creating a rare overlapping view. The overlap allows scientists to study the cosmic dust between the galaxies.
author: NASA News

content:
The Artificial Analysis website has published a new entry for "Gemini 4 Argon (High)," which includes an analysis of the model's intelligence, performance, and price. The article is currently available at the specified URL on the artificialanalysis.ai domain.

title: Furry Airline Pilots Respond to Senator Tommy Tuberville's Rant
content: A member of the furry community responded to recent comments by Senator Tommy Tuberville, asserting that their professional and personal lives are distinct. The individual stated, “We’re furries at home, and we’re airline pilots at work, and these are two separate things,” emphasizing the separation between their identity as airline pilots and their participation in the furry community.
summary: A member of the furry airline pilot community stated that their personal identity and professional duties are separate. This response was made in reaction to recent comments by Senator Tommy Tuberville.
author: Wired

title: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse Compete to Be Your Personal AI Agent
content:
OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse are competing to become the preferred personal AI agent for users. The two products are now emerging as primary contenders in the market for individualized artificial intelligence assistance.

Users are increasingly likely to encounter and utilize both platforms as they seek out dedicated AI agents for their personal use.
summary: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be the preferred AI agent for users. The author has tried both products and suspects readers will do the same.
author: Wired

title: Six AI companies sign voluntary safety accord with White House
content: Six major AI companies signed a voluntary agreement with the White House this week, vowing to implement safeguards. The arrangement is described as a "fancy pinky-swear," raising questions about its practical significance. It remains unclear how much this voluntary accord matters.
summary: Six major AI companies signed a voluntary agreement with the White House this week to implement safeguards. The significance of this commitment remains unclear.
author: Wired

title: White House Aides Less Convinced Than Trump on Republican Midterm Prospects
content:
President Donald Trump maintains that Republican candidates remain competitive in the upcoming midterm elections, according to reports on the White House’s internal outlook. This stance contrasts with the views of his aides, who are reportedly less confident in the party’s chances of success.

The discrepancy in assessment highlights emerging tensions within the administration as the election approaches. While the President continues to express optimism about Republican prospects, his staff appears to be preparing for a more challenging political environment.
summary: President Donald Trump still believes Republicans have a chance in the midterms. His aides are less convinced of this outcome.
author: Wired

title: Asus secures US router ban exemption without confirming manufacturing plans
content:
Asus has secured an exemption from a recent U.S. ban on foreign-made consumer routers, allowing the company to sell its first early Wi-Fi 8 routers in the United States. The ban, implemented this spring, requires foreign manufacturers to prove they are not national security threats and to submit detailed, time-bound plans to establish or expand manufacturing in the U.S. to continue selling products in the country.

As of September 9th, Asus holds this exemption but has not publicly announced any plans to bring manufacturing operations to the United States. The company also declined to confirm to The Verge whether it had submitted a U.S. manufacturing plan as part of the exemption process.
summary: Asus obtained an exemption from the US ban on foreign-made consumer routers to release its first Wi-Fi 8 devices. The company has not publicly announced a plan to establish manufacturing in the United States and refused to confirm if it submitted such a plan.
author: The Verge

title: Verge newsletter Optimizer features recipe for pea-based pesto
content:
Victoria Song, a senior reviewer at The Verge, hosts Optimizer, a weekly newsletter that examines new gadgets and products. In a recent segment, the newsletter featured a video containing a recipe for a pea-based pesto. The video’s narration included the phrase, “I will explode your butthole with this poopmaxxer pesto,” while also noting that the dish does not taste like feces.

The recipe described in the video calls for two cups of blanched peas mixed into a standard pesto preparation, resulting in a yield of 18 grams. The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: Victoria Song's Optimizer newsletter discusses a video featuring a recipe for a pea-based pesto. The recipe combines two cups of blanched peas with standard ingredients to yield 18 grams.
author: The Verge

title: Trump renames AI safety concerns to Super Intelligence after Big Tech meeting
content:
Following a Tuesday dinner with Big Tech leaders, President Donald Trump addressed questions regarding his new artificial intelligence safety plan. He stated that his previous characterization of AI safety concerns as a Democratic "hoax" is no longer accurate, citing the rebranding of the technology as "Super Intelligence." Trump also dismissed worries about insufficient government enforcement of AI guardrails, asserting that U.S. companies are "dominating China."

When asked about the lack of new federal regulations, Trump noted that he now has "the smartest people in the world watching over each other." The article identifies these individuals as leaders from major technology companies, including Google, who attended the meeting.
summary: President Donald Trump stated that previous AI safety fears are no longer applicable because he has renamed the technology to "Super Intelligence." He dismissed calls for federal regulations by asserting that the "smartest people in the world" are currently watching over each other.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Delivery Driver Smart Glasses to Take Thousands of Photos During Shifts
content:
Amazon’s delivery drivers are reportedly set to use smart glasses that capture images "almost constantly" during their shifts. According to a Bloomberg report, the devices could record several thousand photos in a single shift, capturing everything in view, including people and private property. These images are planned to be uploaded to Amazon’s AI Wellspring platform.

In response to inquiries about customer privacy, Amazon’s Viraj Chatterjee stated that the company has not considered allowing customers to opt out of the feature. Chatterjee asserted that the data collected from the glasses is intended solely to "enhance the delivery process," emphasizing that surveillance was never the goal.
summary: Amazon's delivery driver smart glasses will take photos of everything they see, including people and private property, during a typical shift, with several thousand captures expected per driver. The images will be uploaded to Amazon's AI Wellspring platform, and Amazon has not considered an opt‑out option for
author: The Verge

title: Reddit restricts Old Reddit access to combat AI bots
content:
Reddit is implementing stricter access controls for its "Old Reddit" interface to combat scraping and automated traffic. The company recently began requiring users to log in to access the classic experience and announced that, within the next few months, users will also need to have visited Old Reddit within the last six months to continue using it.

According to the announcement, this six-month activity requirement is intended to cover the "vast majority of all Old Reddit users." While the specific details of the enforcement were not fully elaborated, the measure is designed to block both new account creation by bots and existing automated traffic from accessing the platform.
summary: Reddit will require users to have accessed Old Reddit within the last six months to continue using the classic experience. This measure is part of the company's efforts to combat scraping and automated traffic.
author: The Verge

title: Meta and OpenAI to launch AI hardware devices featuring cutesy software agents
content:
Meta and OpenAI are preparing to launch dedicated AI hardware over the next year, aiming to overcome the historical challenges of creating physical devices for artificial intelligence. Both companies are reportedly betting on a similar strategy of testing consumer interest in physical hardware through cutesy software agents, a move intended to change the landscape of AI on phones and computers.

This approach comes despite a history of frustration and backlash surrounding previous dedicated AI devices, such as the Friend and Humane AI Pin. The tech industry often cites "hardware is hard" as a mantra, and public anger toward AI is expected to potentially worsen the reception of these new products.

OpenAI is specifically collaborating with renowned ex-Apple designer Jony Ive on its hardware efforts, as seen in Sam Altman’s appearance at OpenAI’s DevDay 2026.
summary: Meta and OpenAI plan to release dedicated AI devices over the next year, testing consumer demand with physical hardware powered by cutesy software agents. OpenAI is collaborating with ex-Apple designer Jony Ive on its hardware efforts despite past failures of similar devices.
author: The Verge

title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon AI model, initially limited to trusted cyber defenders
content:
Google announced its next AI frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, today. The model is described as delivering “frontier performance in complex workflows across real‑world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense,” according to Koray Kavukcuoglu, chief AI architect and Google DeepMind SVP.

Access to Gemini 4 Argon is initially limited to a “set of trusted cyber defenders.” Kavukcuoglu said Google is “actively engaged in the U. S. Government’s voluntary process for pre‑release model access while we gradually expand access.” He also noted that Gemini 4 Argon is already powering Google’s … (full details available in the original Verge story).
summary: Google announced its new AI frontier model Gemini 4 Argon, which offers frontier performance in complex workflows across real‑world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work such as legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense, according to chief AI architect and Google DeepMind SVP Koray Kavukcuoglu. Access is first restricted to a set of trusted cyber defenders while Google engages in the U.S. Government's voluntary pre‑release model access process and plans to expand access gradually.
author: The Verge

title: Neon Announces SCP Movie, Pledges Creative Commons License After A24's Oversight
content:
Neon has announced it is developing an SCP Foundation movie, a move that contrasts sharply with A24’s recent project. A24 reportedly angered the online horror community by announcing its film without contacting the SCP Wiki team or committing to release the content under a Creative Commons license. In response, Neon proactively reached out to the SCP Foundation Wiki team and pledged to release its film under the Creative Commons ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) license.

The new project is not an official SCP film. No members of the wiki staff are involved in the writing or production, and the team is not receiving compensation for the project.
summary: Neon announced it is making an SCP Foundation movie and has reached out to the SCP Foundation Wiki team. Neon pledged to release the film under the Creative Commons ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) license, while A24 had announced a film without contacting the Wiki team or committing to the license.
author: The Verge

title: Google's AI payment scheme struggles as sites earn minimal revenue
content:
Google's initial effort to compensate websites for providing answers to AI queries is facing significant challenges. The program has failed to generate meaningful income for the participating publishers.

Currently, many sites report receiving only one-tenth of one percent of their total advertising revenue from these AI-related payments.
summary: Many sites receive only a tiny fraction of their advertising revenue from AI payments. The share is just one-tenth of one percent.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nonprofit sues OpenAI over Hugging Face hack, says 'An AI did it' is no defense
content:
A nonprofit organization is suing OpenAI, arguing that the company’s claim that "An AI did it" is an invalid defense against liability for the Hugging Face hack. The lawsuit contends that OpenAI’s actions have resulted in negative consequences for other parties.

The nonprofit alleges that OpenAI makes others suffer "the harms of its unsafe decision-making." This assertion forms the core of the legal challenge against the artificial intelligence developer regarding the security incident involving Hugging Face.
summary: A nonprofit is suing OpenAI over a Hugging Face hack, saying 'An AI did it' is no defense. The nonprofit claims OpenAI causes others to suffer 'the harms of its unsafe decision‑making'.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump Secures Voluntary AI Safety Tests from Dozens of Firms
content:
President Trump has secured agreements from dozens of artificial intelligence companies to participate in voluntary safety testing. This initiative forms the core of the administration's strategy to address potential risks associated with AI development.

The plan relies on major technology firms to self-regulate and conduct these assessments without mandatory government enforcement. By engaging industry leaders directly, the approach aims to manage AI risks through collaborative efforts rather than strict regulatory mandates.
summary: Trump has secured agreements from dozens of AI firms to conduct voluntary safety tests. The initiative involves voluntary testing by the firms.
author: Ars Technica

title: RFK Jr. says AI will free us from "tyranny" of medical facts
content:
RFK Jr. has said that artificial intelligence could free society from what he calls the “tyranny” of medical facts and expertise.

He acknowledges that AI is far from a perfect resource, noting its limitations.

In a comparison he points out that AI appears to hallucinate less than Kennedy.
summary: RFK Jr. believes artificial intelligence will liberate people from the "tyranny" of medical facts and expertise. The provided text notes that AI is far from a perfect resource but hallucinates less than Kennedy.

title: OpenAI’s Decisions API, a Jev clone, may help Frontier Lab stop swarming agents
content:
OpenAI’s new “Decisions API” is a Jev clone that underscores the importance of fast, cheap intelligence. The tool is positioned as a rapid decision‑making engine that can process information quickly and at low cost.

According to the announcement, the Jev clone could help the frontier lab stop its swarming agents, offering a potential solution for controlling autonomous agent behavior.
summary: OpenAI’s Decisions API is a Jev clone that confirms the importance of fast, cheap intelligence. The API could help the Frontier Lab stop its swarming agents.

title: BMW 3 Series: Gas and Electric Models Built Same, EV $4,400 Cheaper
content:
BMW has produced the same model for both gasoline and electric powertrains, with the electric version priced $4,400 lower than its gasoline counterpart.  

The new BMW 3 Series illustrates how rapidly electric vehicles are narrowing the price gap with fossil‑fuel vehicles.  

The new BMW 3 Series demonstrates the price convergence between EV and gas models.
summary: BMW built the same car for gas and electric. The electric version is $4,400 cheaper, showing how quickly EVs have caught up to fossil fuel vehicles on pricing.
author: TechCrunch

title: DoorDash unveils six-propeller aircraft for new drone delivery at Dash Forward 2026
content:
DoorDash announced the launch of its new drone delivery initiative by unveiling a six‑propeller aircraft at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event.

The aircraft will serve as the core vehicle for DoorDash’s planned drone‑based delivery service, marking the company’s first step toward expanding its logistics capabilities beyond ground‑based options.
summary: DoorDash unveiled the six‑propeller aircraft that will be used in its new drone delivery business. The unveiling occurred at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event.
author: TechCrunch

title: Hackers Steal Millions of US Military Personnel Records in Months-Long Breach
content:
Hackers stole millions of U. S. military personnel records during a months‑long data breach, according to a recent report.

The Department of Defense notified millions of current and former U. S. military personnel that their personal information had been stolen in the breach.
summary: Department of Defense notified millions of current and former U.S. military personnel that their personal information had been stolen. The breach lasted months.
author: TechCrunch

title: Spotify founder Daniel Ek's Neko Health raises $700M for body scan startup
content:
Spotify founder Daniel Ek’s startup Neko Health has raised $700 million to develop a body‑scan technology aimed at preventative healthcare. The funding will support the company’s plans to build a business around scanning users’ bodies.

The body‑scan focus is not unique to Neko Health. Midjourney is also building its own body scanner, and Function Health has secured significant capital to expand its preventative‑health platform.

These developments were discussed on an episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast.
summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek’s Neko Health raised $700 million to build a body‑scan business. Midjourney and Function Health are also developing body scanners and preventative‑health platforms.
author: TechCrunch

title: VC Chris Degnan Leaves Factory AI to Become Cognition's Chief Revenue Officer
content:
The CEO of Factory AI has publicly accused former board advisor Chris Degnan of spying for the rival firm Cognition.  

Degnan, a venture capitalist, previously served as a board advisor to Factory AI before accepting a position as chief revenue officer at Cognition.  

No further details have been released.

title: Flow Engineering raised $750M valuation backed by Valor, Atreides, Sequoia
content:
Flow Engineering has been valued at $750 million after receiving backing from Valor, Atreides, and Sequoia.  

The AI startup is focused on bringing AI agents to hardware design. In addition to the new funding, Flow Engineering has secured Roelof Botha as an angel investor and board member.  

The investment brings the startup to a $750 million valuation.
summary: Flow Engineering, a startup that brings AI agents to hardware design, raised a $750M valuation with backing from Valor, Atreides, and Sequoia. The company also secured Roelof Botha as an angel investor and board member.
author: TechCrunch

title: FTC Launches Investigation into Anthropic, OpenAI and Other AI Labs
content:
The Federal Trade Commission has launched an industry‑wide investigation into several artificial‑intelligence laboratories, including Anthropic and OpenAI. The probe is the first official U.S. enforcement action targeting so‑called rogue AI agents.  

The investigation aims to uncover potential dangers that the technology may pose to consumers. It follows a surge in incidents first reported in July, which have heightened public concerns that uncontrolled AI could one day harm humans.
summary: The Federal Trade Commission is conducting an industry‑wide investigation into Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI labs to uncover potential dangers their technology poses to consumers. This investigation is the first official US enforcement action that delves into rogue AI agents, following a surge in incidents first reported in July that have stoked fears among the public that uncontrolled AI could one day harm humans.
