title: Ethiopia's government and Tigray clash erupts, raising Horn of Africa spillover fears
content:
Ethiopia back to civil war? Horn of Africa fears spillover effect of renewed fighting

After contagion in the Arabian Peninsula, should the entire Horn of Africa fear a domino effect? The article draws a parallel between Donald Trump’s decision to invade Iran, which drew the Saudis back to Yemen, and the situation in Ethiopia, where unresolved issues between the government and its Tigray region erupted last week.

The piece asks whether threats over the Strait of Bab el‑Mandeb could have lit the fuse for renewed fighting in Ethiopia. It questions whether a potential return to civil war could draw in regional rivals.

The article ends by posing the question of whether the renewed conflict in Ethiopia might trigger a broader regional crisis.
summary: Unresolved issues between Ethiopia's government and its Tigray region erupted last week. Observers fear the fighting could spread across the Horn of Africa and involve regional rivals.
author: France 24

title: French teens clash with police as school blockades intensify, hundreds detained
content:
French teenagers clashed with police on Tuesday, setting fire to rubbish bins and hurling projectiles. Police responded with batons and tear‑gas, and hundreds of youths were detained nationwide amid escalating school blockades and protests demanding better school conditions.

The unrest follows a wave of demonstrations that began last week, with students gathering outside hundreds of schools to protest issues such as timetables, class sizes, a shortage of teachers and overheated classrooms during this year’s heatwaves. FRANCE 24’s Rachel Griffiths reported.
summary: French teenagers set fire to rubbish bins and threw projectiles at police, who responded with batons and tear gas, leading to hundreds of detentions nationwide. The protests, ongoing since last week, involve blockades outside hundreds of schools over timetables, class sizes, teacher shortages and overheated classrooms.
author: France 24

title: Cristiano Ronaldo quits Portugal training camp after being dropped for Denmark match
content:
Portugal captain and striker Cristiano Ronaldo said on Wednesday that he left the national team’s training camp in Copenhagen after coach Jorge Jesus announced the 41‑year‑old would be omitted from Portugal’s upcoming match against Denmark.

Ronaldo confirmed he walked out of the camp following the decision to drop him from the squad for the Denmark game.
summary: Portugal captain and striker Cristiano Ronaldo said he walked out of the national team’s training camp in Copenhagen. Coach Jorge Jesus announced the 41‑year‑old would be dropped from Portugal’s next match against Denmark.
author: France 24

title: Expert says Manchester City likely to face full penalties for financial rule breaches
content:
Manchester City’s rapid ascent from a mid‑table side to Premier League dominance has been clouded by a finding that the club breached a series of financial rules. The violations could jeopardise the team’s recent success, according to the report.

FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen interviewed James Reade, a Professor of Economics at the University of Reading, who said the club is unlikely to receive any leniency from football authorities. “It’s hard to see it getting anything other than the book thrown at them,” Reade said.
summary: Manchester City were found guilty of scores of financial rule breaches, putting their recent Premier League dominance at risk. Professor James Reade, a University of Reading economics professor, said it is hard to see the club receiving any leniency from football authorities.
author: France 24

title: Trump’s “America” AI chatbot shifts from challenging to refusing his claims
content:
Donald Trump has launched “America,” a chatbot designed as a digital portal for U.S. government information. The tool was introduced to provide citizens with direct access to official data and resources.

Initially, the chatbot challenged several of Trump’s claims, including statements about the 2020 election and inflation, and supplied evidence and links to support its responses. In recent tests, the chatbot has refused to answer some of the same questions, while other replies still contradict Trump’s positions and some echo his views.

Vedika Bahl tested the chatbot, noting its varying answers in the Truth or Fake assessment.
summary: Donald Trump launched “America,” an AI chatbot designed as a digital portal for U.S. government information. The bot’s responses have changed, initially challenging several of Trump’s claims about the 2020 election and inflation with evidence and links, then later refusing to answer some of the same questions while still offering both contradictory and supportive replies.
author: France 24

title: Ethiopian AI ethicist Timnit Gebru receives Swedish Right Livelihood Award
content:
Ethiopian‑born computer scientist and pioneering AI ethicist Timnit Gebru was honored with the Swedish Right Livelihood Award for her research on how artificial‑intelligence systems are shaped by biases. The award, often referred to as the “alternative Nobel,” recognized her contributions to exposing and addressing bias in AI technologies. 

Gebru’s work has highlighted the ways in which machine‑learning models can perpetuate inequities, prompting broader discussions about ethical standards in the field. The Right Livelihood Award ceremony marked a significant acknowledgment of her influence on AI ethics worldwide.
summary: Timnit Gebru, an Ethiopian-born computer scientist and pioneering AI ethicist, was honored with the Swedish Right Livelihood Award. The award recognized her work on how AI is influenced by biases.
author: France 24

title: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham revives debate on Britain rejoining EU
content:
Andy Burnham, the United Kingdom’s prime minister, raised the prospect of Britain rejoining the European Union on Wednesday, a move that broke a long‑standing taboo for a UK prime minister and reopened the divisive Brexit debate.  

During an interview with FRANCE 24’s Monte Francis, Burnham articulated the idea. Catherine Barnard, Professor of European Law at the University of Cambridge, noted that Burnham’s remarks signal that “it’s been pretty cold being on the outside of the EU, so we’re now looking at the alternatives.”  

The discussion has reignited debate over the UK’s relationship with the EU.
summary: Andy Burnham put the idea of Britain rejoining the EU on the table Wednesday, breaking a taboo for a UK prime minister. In an interview with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Cambridge law professor Catherine Barnard said Burnham is signaling that being outside the EU feels cold and alternatives are being considered.
author: France 24

title: Unclear how Saudi Arabia can counter Houthi threat in Yemen as US and Europe stay distant
content:
Uncertainty surrounds Saudi Arabia’s capacity to neutralize the threat posed by Yemen’s Houthi forces. Analysts note that the Saudis lack a clear strategy for defusing the insurgent group operating in neighboring Yemen.

The United States has shown little interest in intervening, European nations are described as hedging, and no party appears willing to engage in an open conflict with Iran.
summary: It is unclear how Saudi Arabia can defuse the threat presented by the Houthis in Yemen. The United States is not interested, European nations are hedging, and no party wants open conflict with Iran.

title: Five EU countries aim to open first deportation center in Africa by 2027
content:
Five EU states plan the first deportation center in Africa for 2027. Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers outside the EU.

An African partner country has reportedly already been selected to host the facility. The initiative is part of the five countries’ joint effort to create a new deportation center outside the European Union.
summary: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers outside the EU. An African partner country has reportedly already been selected.
author: DW World

title: UNICEF says one in five Lebanese children go to bed hungry
content:
Lebanon: One in five children goes to bed hungry, says UNICEF

UNICEF reports that four in five households in Lebanon are struggling to afford basic necessities, with children increasingly going without food, missing school, and being pushed into work as conflict compounds years of economic crisis. The agency cited a father of four on Wednesday who said, “I wanted to buy clothes for my children, but I could not. I also wanted to enrol them in school, but I could not afford that either.”
summary: UNICEF says one in five children in Lebanon go to bed hungry. Four in five households struggle to afford basic necessities, with children increasingly missing food, school and being pushed into work.
author: UN News

title: UNHCR Calls for Safeguards After Malaysia Sends 1,476 Refugees Back to Myanmar
content: The United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) has expressed concern over Malaysia’s decision to send 1,476 people back to Myanmar. The agency warned that the returns occur while the country remains engulfed in a civil war and faces a dire human‑rights and humanitarian situation.
summary: UNHCR has voiced concern over Malaysia’s decision to return 1,476 people to Myanmar. The return occurs amid an ongoing civil war and a dire human rights and humanitarian situation.
author: UN News

title: Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked
content:
A United Nations report released on Wednesday says homicide rates are declining across much of the world, even as organised crime expands in many regions.  

The study notes that criminal networks are becoming more profitable and increasingly networked, diversifying into activities such as trafficking, migrant smuggling and the exploitation of natural resources. The UN report was launched on Wednesday.
summary: Homicide rates are falling across much of the world, but organised crime is on the rise in many regions as criminal networks diversify into trafficking, migrant smuggling, and the exploitation of natural resources, a new…
author: UN News

title: Proposed global panel to tackle inequality with scientific firepower
content:
A new global panel is being proposed as a possible mechanism to confront rising inequality, with the idea that it could apply the same level of scientific coordination that has been mobilized for the climate crisis. The concept suggests treating inequality as a “ticking time bomb” that might be defused through coordinated research and policy efforts.

Advocates of the panel argue that leveraging scientific firepower—data analysis, modeling and interdisciplinary collaboration—could provide the evidence‑based strategies needed to reduce disparities worldwide, mirroring the approach taken to address climate change.
summary: An article asks whether a new global panel could be created to defuse inequality’s “ticking time bomb.” It suggests applying the scientific firepower used for the climate crisis to address inequality.
author: UN News

title: UN teams race to shield Gaza families from rainy season amid access, supply shortages
content:
UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, according to UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric.  

The effort is hampered by restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies, Dujarric said on Wednesday.  

No further details were provided.
summary: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season. Their effort is hampered by restricted land access and shortages of critical supplies, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday.
author: UN News

title: FTC probes AI firms over rogue agent risks and potential humanity threats
content:
The Federal Trade Commission has opened an investigation into artificial‑intelligence companies, according to the announcement that the U.S. regulator is launching a probe into AI firms.

The FTC’s inquiry focuses on concerns that rogue agents could emerge from AI technologies and pose potential threats to humanity within the next decade. The agency is examining whether these risks warrant further regulatory action.
summary: The FTC has opened an investigation into AI companies. The probe is driven by concerns about rogue agents and possible threats to humanity within the next decade.

title: Gas pipeline explosion in Syria disables three power plants, prompts higher power rationing
content:
A gas pipeline explosion in Syria has taken three power plants offline, officials said. The blast disrupted electricity generation across the affected area.

In response, authorities announced that power‑rationing hours will be increased to compensate for the loss of supply. The adjustment aims to manage the reduced electricity availability following the incident.
summary: A gas pipeline exploded in Syria, knocking three power plants offline. Power rationing hours are to increase as a result of the blast.

title: Trekkers evacuated by helicopter as deadly landslides kill about 30 in Nepal
content:
Trekkers in Nepal were evacuated by helicopter from mountainous terrain as a new wave of deadly landslides struck the region. The rescues came amid reports that landslides and heavy rain continued to threaten hikers and local communities.

A month after a mass catastrophic flooding event, around 30 people have died in landslides and heavy rain, according to the latest figures.
summary: Trekkers were helicoptered off the mountains in Nepal. Around 30 people have died in landslides and heavy rain a month after mass catastrophic flooding.

content:
SpaceX achieved a significant milestone in the Starship program during Flight 14, with the vehicle reaching orbit. The launch involved Booster 21, which experienced a loss during the mission.

title: Pussycat Dolls trio tour opens in Birmingham after legal disputes
content:
The Pussycat Dolls launched their comeback tour at the Utilita Arena in Birmingham, performing as a trio consisting of Nicole Scherzinger, Ashley Roberts, and Kimberly Wyatt. The reunion, originally announced in 2019 with nearly the full original lineup, was previously canceled due to the pandemic and a legal dispute. After years of silence, the group shared plans for a 53-date world tour, although poor ticket sales resulted in the cancellation of the US leg.

Tensions surrounding the reunion have included allegations from former member Jessica Sutta, who claimed she was excluded because she was viewed as a “liability” due to her support for Maga; the group did not comment on the claim. On stage, the trio delivered a nearly two-hour performance characterized by synchronized choreography, hair-flipping, and booty-shaking. The setlist included hits such as “When I Grow Up,” “Beep,” and “I Don’t Need a Man,” with Scherzinger handling lead vocals following her recent Tony award-winning run on Broadway in Sunset Blvd.

Roberts and Wyatt also received solo moments during the show, notably during “Wait a Minute,” which featured pots-and-pans percussion. The performance highlighted the group’s history of fierce dance routines, which defined their initial 2005-09 run that produced six UK Top 3 hits.
summary: The Pussycat Dolls launched their 53-date world tour as a trio of Nicole Scherzinger, Ashley Roberts, and Kimberly Wyatt at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. This reunion follows a fraught history that includes a 2019 announcement, pandemic delays, a legal dispute, and allegations from former member Jessica Sutta.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film focuses on gameplay mechanics over familiar characters
content:
Zach Cregger’s cinematic adaptation of the Resident Evil series has sparked debate among fans who criticize the film for omitting iconic characters like Leon, Claire, and Ada Wong. Despite the absence of these familiar figures and well-known locations, the article argues that Cregger’s interpretation is one of the most accurate video game films ever made by focusing on the fundamental experience of playing the original game.

The plot centers on Bryan Hodukavich, a courier who is thrust into a viral outbreak in Raccoon City after the Umbrella Corporation accidentally releases a zombifying virus. Without weapons or knowledge of the situation, Bryan navigates a series of locations drawn directly from the games, including an abandoned farmhouse, a tunnel filled with cars, a hospital, and a sewer level.

Throughout the film, the protagonist encounters escalating peril and body horror while acquiring increasingly powerful weapons, such as a handgun and an assault rifle, though he remains short on ammunition. The adaptation also includes specific narrative conveniences from the source material, such as typewriters appearing in at least two scenes.
summary: Zach Cregger's cinematic adaptation of Resident Evil excludes familiar heroes such as Leon, Claire, and Ada Wong. Instead, the film replicates the game's structural conventions by following a courier through familiar locations with limited weapons and ammunition.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jean-Pierre Laffont’s photo of the Savage Skulls, the most dangerous gang in the Bronx
content:
French photographer Jean-Pierre Laffont, who moved to New York from France in 1965, documented the city’s gang violence during the late 1960s and 1970s. After establishing himself as the first foreign correspondent for the Paris-based Gamma Agency in 1969, Laffont prioritized personal projects over standard assignments. In 1972, he began following reports in the New York Times about gangs in the Bronx targeting drug-pushers who preyed on young people.

Laffont noted that police frequently discovered the victims’ bodies on the kerbs at the bottom of five-storey buildings, where they had been thrown. While the area featured several gangs, including the Savage Nomads and the Dirty Dozen, Laffont identified the Savage Skulls as the most dangerous group. He stated that he did not want to search for the victims alone due to the hazardous conditions in the city, particularly at night.
summary: French photographer Jean-Pierre Laffont documented the Savage Skulls, a gang in the Bronx that killed drug-pushers targeting young people. He noted that police found the victims' bodies at the bottom of five-storey buildings where they had been thrown.
author: Guardian Culture

content:

title: Kevin and Jack Sinfield face diverging paths to Super League Grand Final
content:
The Sinfield family is set to feature in the Super League Grand Final, with father Kevin and son Jack pursuing diverging paths to the title match. While Leeds has served as the focal point of their rugby story for over 20 years, attention has shifted 10 miles to Wakefield this week as Jack aims to secure his first title with the Wakefield Trinity Wildcats.

Kevin Sinfield recently completed an ultramarathon challenge, finishing in time for the kick-off at Old Trafford. This personal feat coincides with his son’s bid for a major championship, highlighting a week of significant sporting milestones for the family.
summary: Kevin Sinfield's ultramarathon challenge concludes in time for the kick-off at Old Trafford, while his son Jack aims for a first title with Wakefield. The family's focus has shifted from Leeds to Wakefield as they prepare for the upcoming Super League Grand Final.

title: Guardiola backs Manchester City owners after guilty verdict on financial rules
content:
Pep Guardiola has voiced his support for Manchester City following the club’s guilty verdict on all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period. The former manager, who left the club in the summer after a decade in charge, told fans, “We will get through this together,” while adding, “I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club.”

Guardiola’s first two seasons at Manchester City fell within the timeframe investigated by the independent commission. He remains a close ally of chief executive Ferran Soriano, who brought him to England, as the two previously worked together at Barcelona.

Despite the verdict, Manchester City maintains its innocence and is set to appeal against the decision before Friday’s deadline. Former City chair Bernstein has called on directors to quit in response to the outcome.
summary: Pep Guardiola expressed his continued support for Manchester City after the club was found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period. The club maintains its innocence and is set to appeal against the decision before Friday's deadline.

content:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened an investigation into former Representative Adam Kinzinger (R-Ill.) concerning trades on the prediction market platform Kalshi. The inquiry focuses on transactions related to pardons issued by former President Biden.

content:
JMSN’s legal team has sent a cease-and-desist letter to the White House, demanding the removal of the R&B artist’s song "Love Me" from a controversial advertisement. The music is featured prominently in a government-funded commercial that highlights President Trump’s political agenda.

content: An entrepreneur argues that critics of Flock Safety’s automated license plate reading technology incorrectly equate the mere collection of data with its potential for misuse. The perspective suggests that such tools should be evaluated based on the philosophy of the individuals or entities using them, rather than being subject to outright bans.
summary: An entrepreneur states that opponents of Flock Safety's automated license plate reading technology mistakenly equate data collection with potential misuse. The author suggests these tools should be judged by the philosophy of their users rather than banned outright.

title: Newsom calls himself a 'disrupter at heart' in Vanity Fair interview
content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom (D) described himself as a political “disrupter at heart” in a series of interviews with Vanity Fair published Wednesday. The remarks come as the Democratic state leader publicly weighs a presidential bid for 2028.

In the interviews, Newsom also addressed the recent surge of support for democratic socialist candidates during the current midterm election cycle.
summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom described himself as a political "disrupter" in a series of interviews with Vanity Fair. The interviews were published as the Democratic state leader publicly weighs a presidential bid in 2028.

title: Fed watchdog finds no criminality in Powell renovation probe
content:
The Federal Reserve’s internal watchdog concluded in a Wednesday report that former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and other Fed officials did not violate criminal law during their management of the central bank’s ongoing multimillion-dollar renovation project. The finding was issued by the office of Fed Inspector General Michael Horowitz.

While the report cleared the officials of criminal misconduct, it acknowledged that the Federal Reserve "has not effectively executed" the construction management risk contract associated with the renovation.
summary: The Fed's Inspector General reported that Jerome Powell and officials did not violate criminal law during the central bank's renovation project. The office acknowledged that the Fed has not effectively executed the construction management risk contract.

title: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to outline Pentagon shake‑up in State of the Force address
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to deliver the annual State of the Force address on Wednesday, where he will outline his priorities for the U.S. Military. The speech arrives amid efforts by Hegseth to implement a significant reorganization within the Pentagon.

During the address, Hegseth is expected to announce plans to reduce the number of general and admiral positions by 20 percent, a move that would double a previous reduction.
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will present his priorities for the U.S. military during the State of the Force address on Wednesday. He is expected to announce a plan to cut the number of general and admiral positions by 20 percent, doubling a reduction.

title: Senate Democrats block Ratepayer Protection Act over data center costs
content:
Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act on Wednesday in a procedural vote, denying the legislation the 60 votes required to overcome the filibuster. The Democrats characterized the bill as ineffective and “toothless,” opposing its passage despite its prior approval in the House.

The legislation, which aims to address electricity costs associated with data centers, had previously passed the House with significant bipartisan support.
summary: Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act by failing to provide the 60 votes needed to overcome the filibuster. They described the legislation, which passed the House with bipartisan support, as ineffective and "toothless."

content:
The Justice Department on Wednesday announced it is seeking to censure two federal judges in Minnesota after they spoke to The New York Times about the Trump administration’s immigration surge in the state.  

The judges targeted are former Judge Patrick Schiltz, a George W. Bush appointee, and sitting Judge John Tunheim.

content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer has expressed significant concern regarding the potential sale of Manchester City following allegations of rule breaches. content:
Simone Rossi, the head of EDF Energy, stated that developing new oil and gas projects in the North Sea is a “no-brainer” that poses “no contradiction” to net zero goals. Rossi’s comments align with a broader argument made by other renewables leaders advocating for increased North Sea production.

These statements come as the government prepares to make decisions on two specific projects in the region.

title: Sylvester Center researchers create AI framework for cancer survivorship support
content:
Researchers at Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, have developed a framework for creating, evaluating, and implementing artificial intelligence tools in cancer survivorship and supportive care. This initiative aims to provide personalized support to cancer survivors between doctor visits.

The details of this new framework were presented in a proof-of-concept study recently published in the journal Translational Behavioral Medicine.
summary: Researchers at Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center developed a framework for creating and evaluating AI tools in cancer survivorship. This proof-of-concept study was published in the journal Translational Behavioral Medicine.

title: Wits PHR researchers urge WHO to declare climate crisis a public health emergency
content: Researchers from Wits Planetary Health Research (Wits PHR) at the University of the Witwatersrand, along with international partner institutions, have called on the World Health Organization (WHO) and its member states to formally declare the climate crisis a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC). The group argues that the immediate health impacts of the climate crisis necessitate a globally coordinated response to protect the health of the most vulnerable populations.
summary: Researchers from Wits Planetary Health Research (Wits PHR), University of the Witwatersrand, and international partner institutions are calling on the World Health Organization (WHO) and its member states to formally declare the climate crisis a public health emergency of international concern. They argue that the climate crisis's immediate health impacts require a globally coordinated response to safeguard the health of the most vulnerable.
author: Medical Xpress

title: TIGEM study identifies druggable pathway to activate TFEB for lysosomal diseases
content:
A study published in Nature by scientists at the Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM) has identified a molecular pathway that regulates TFEB activity. This discovery reveals new druggable targets that could facilitate the development of therapies for conditions linked to lysosomal dysfunction, including rare genetic diseases and cancer.

TFEB has long been considered a promising therapeutic target for restoring the cell’s ability to clear and recycle waste. However, translating this potential into actual treatments has been challenging because TFEB itself is difficult to target with drugs. The newly identified pathway offers a route to overcome this obstacle by providing alternative molecular targets for intervention.
summary: A study by TIGEM scientists published in Nature identified a molecular pathway that controls TFEB activity, providing new druggable targets. These targets could enable therapies for rare genetic diseases, cancer, and other conditions linked to lysosomal dysfunction.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Newly uncovered enzyme mechanism could help target drug-resistant breast cancer
content:
Boston Children's Hospital researchers and colleagues have identified a new mechanism driving resistance in hormone receptor positive (HR+) breast cancer, the most common subtype of the disease. The study addresses the significant clinical challenge of treatment resistance emerging in these patients.

The discovery points to potential methods for detecting resistant cancer cells at an early stage and offers a possible strategy for targeting them.
summary: Boston Children's Hospital researchers and colleagues discovered a new driver of resistance in hormone receptor positive breast cancer. This finding points to a way to detect resistant cancer cells early and a possible method to target them.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links parenting profiles to children's behavioral and emotional problems
content:
A new study published in PLOS One identified data-driven profiles of parenting practices to investigate their association with children's behavioral and emotional problems. The research examines how different patterns of parenting relate to these issues, noting that there is no single correct way to raise a child.

The study categorizes the observed problems into two main groups: internalizing behaviors, such as withdrawal, anxiety, and depression, and externalizing behaviors, including aggression, oppositional behavior, and attention problems.
summary: A study published in PLOS One identified data-driven profiles of parenting practices and investigated their association with children's behavioral and emotional problems. These problems are generally grouped into internalizing behaviors, such as anxiety, and externalizing behaviors, such as aggression.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Speech-based machine learning clocks estimate age and brain health
content:
A large study indicates that machine-learning models based on speech can estimate an individual's chronological age. These "voice clocks" may also provide insights into brain aging, biological aging, and cognitive health.

The research suggests that vocal characteristics could reflect broader physiological changes, including cumulative burden and the presence of dementia. This approach offers a potential non-invasive method for assessing various aspects of aging and cognitive decline.
summary: A large study indicates that machine-learning clocks based on speech can estimate chronological age. These tools may also provide insights into brain aging, biological aging, cognitive health, and dementia.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UMass Amherst team develops wearable stroke rehab device with machine learning
content:
A research team led by University of Massachusetts Amherst scientists has developed a wearable wrist device that utilizes a machine-learning algorithm to continuously track changes in arm movement impairment following a stroke. The technology is designed to monitor these changes throughout the rehabilitation process.

By providing continuous data, the device could enable clinicians to adjust therapy in real time. This approach aims to tailor patient care rather than relying on the current one-size-fits-all method.
summary: Researchers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst created a wearable wrist device that uses a machine-learning algorithm to track arm movement impairment after a stroke. This technology allows clinicians to adjust therapy in real time, moving away from a one-size-fits-all approach to rehabilitation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Eli Lilly to Start Phase 3 Trials for Tirzepatide and Eloralintide Combo
content: Eli Lilly announced that its combination obesity regimen, which pairs the amylin drug eloralintide with tirzepatide, demonstrated increased weight loss in a mid-stage clinical trial. The pharmaceutical company stated that it intends to initiate Phase 3 trials for this combination therapy by the end of the year.
summary: Eli Lilly announced that its combination obesity regimen of tirzepatide and eloralintide boosts weight loss in mid-stage trials. The company plans to begin Phase 3 trials for this regimen at the end of the year.

title: Report: Polar oceans transformed as warming melts ice habitats
content: An annual report released Wednesday indicates that climate change is significantly altering the polar oceans. The findings highlight that Arctic waters are experiencing rapid warming, which is contributing to a substantial reduction in sea ice. Consequently, wildlife at both the North and South Poles are losing critical habitat as the environment shifts.
summary: An annual report states that climate change is increasingly reshaping the polar oceans. Arctic waters are warming rapidly, causing sea ice to shrink and wildlife to lose habitat at both ends of the planet.
author: Phys.org

title: Zinc oxide quantum dots achieve faster charge detection, advancing spin qubit research
content:
Zinc oxide quantum dots enable faster charge detection, laying groundwork for spin qubits. Researchers at Tohoku University, in collaboration with the National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS) and the University of Tokyo, have used zinc oxide (ZnO) quantum dots to achieve a significant improvement in charge detection speed. This advancement is an important step toward developing semiconductor quantum computing technologies that rely on ZnO.

The work demonstrates that ZnO quantum dots can serve as a platform for spin‑based qubits, potentially accelerating progress in quantum computing research.
summary: Researchers at Tohoku University, the National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS) and the University of Tokyo reported that zinc oxide quantum dots enable faster charge detection. The work is described as an important step toward semiconductor quantum computing using spin qubits.
author: Phys.org

title: 19 Charged in Interstate Scheme to Steal Used Cooking Oil
content:
Federal prosecutors revealed an interstate criminal enterprise involving the theft of used cooking oil, a scheme characterized by clandestine warehouses, money laundering, and the transport of stolen goods across state lines. The announcement, made in mid-September 2026, detailed a network operating with the hallmarks of organized crime.

A total of 19 defendants face charges in the case. Two of the accused have already pleaded guilty, while the remaining defendants are scheduled to go to trial in April 2027.
summary: Federal prosecutors announced a mid-September 2026 indictment of 19 defendants for an interstate criminal enterprise involving the theft of used cooking oil. Two defendants have pleaded guilty, while the remaining 17 are scheduled for trial in April 2027.

title: 2026 Nor'easter Storm Surge Floods U.S. Atlantic Coast
content: A powerful nor'easter struck the U.S. Atlantic coast in late September 2026, causing ocean water to flood coastal neighborhoods from North Carolina to New York. The storm surge and heavy rainfall filled streets and surrounded homes, while near-hurricane-force winds knocked out power. The event may have also uncovered a shipwreck that is more than a century old.
summary: A powerful nor'easter struck the U.S. Atlantic coast in late September 2026, causing ocean water to flood coastal neighborhoods from North Carolina to New York. The storm surge, heavy rain, and near-hurricane-force winds filled streets, surrounded homes, and knocked out power.

title: University of Oldenburg physicists generate 3D light fields to reach new quantum states
content: A team of physicists at the University of Oldenburg has generated three-dimensional light fields by superimposing two ultrashort laser pulses that converge from different directions. This technique allows researchers to push electrons into quantum states that were previously beyond experimental reach.
summary: A team of physicists at the University of Oldenburg generated three-dimensional light fields by superimposing two ultrashort laser pulses converging from different directions. This technique pushed electrons into quantum states that were previously beyond experimental reach.

title: La Trobe finds 18 fossils confirming 2-million-year-old Homo erectus in southern Africa
content: La Trobe archaeologists have identified 18 new hominin fossils, including a second Homo erectus skull fragment. This discovery confirms that the species first appeared in southern Africa 2.0 million years ago. This timeline places the emergence of Homo erectus in the region 200,000 years earlier than previously established.
summary: La Trobe archaeologists described 18 new hominin fossils, including a second Homo erectus skull fragment. This discovery confirms the species first appeared in southern Africa 2.0 million years ago, which is 200,000 years earlier than traditionally thought.

title: EU poverty declined 2015-2023 despite national disparities, study finds
content: A study published in PLOS One reports that poverty levels in the European Union decreased between 2015 and 2023. The research was conducted by Silvia Megyesiova and Cecilia Olexova from the Bratislava University of Economics and Business in Košice, Slovak Republic. While the overall trend showed a decline, the study notes that significant disparities in poverty rates persist among the member nations.
summary: A study published in PLOS One reports that poverty in the European Union declined between 2015 and 2023. The research by Silvia Megyesiova and Cecilia Olexova notes that significant disparities persist among EU nations.

title: Judy Wearing's book explores evolution and culture of human hair
content:
Judy Wearing’s new book, Anxious and Hairy, explores the evolution and culture of human hair, addressing the biological and cultural reasons why humans have hair on their heads and other parts of their bodies. The work is described as an enthusiastic and curious dive into these topics.

Elle Hunt, who was initially skeptical of the subject matter, has been captivated by Wearing’s exploration of the topic.

content: Medications and pills are often viewed as the most rigorous methods for treating illness, yet emerging understanding suggests that healthcare must address the entire mind and body. summary: Pills and other medications are often seen as the most rigorous way to treat illness. Increasingly, health is understood to require attention to the whole mind and body.

title: New AI system defeats top human players at Stratego
content:
A new AI system has emerged as the leading performer in the board game Stratego, demonstrating the ability to defeat top-ranked human players. The system is noted for being more efficient than other existing models in handling the game's complex decision-making processes.

Developers suggest this advanced capability could extend beyond gaming, potentially assisting decision-makers in high-stakes scenarios such as military maneuvers or business negotiations.
summary: The new game-playing AI is able to defeat top-ranked human players at Stratego. It is more efficient than other models and could help decision-makers in military maneuvers or business negotiations.

title: Ocean heatwaves are hiding months of extra warming
content:
Marine heatwaves represent only the peak intensity of broader warming events, as elevated ocean temperatures often persist for months beyond the initial peak. This extended duration means that traditional monitoring methods fail to capture the full scope of thermal stress experienced by marine environments.

Recent research indicates that conventional measurements underestimate total heat exposure by an average of more than 150%. By ignoring the lingering warmth after the main event, these standard metrics overlook a significant source of stress on marine ecosystems.
summary: Marine heatwaves may be only the most intense part of much longer warming events, with elevated temperatures sometimes lingering for months. Researchers found that conventional measurements underestimate total heat exposure by more than 150% on average, potentially overlooking a major source of stress on marine ecosystems.
author: Science Daily

title: Genomic study suggests bats first evolved in Europe 65–60 million years ago
content:
A new genomic and fossil study suggests that bats first evolved in Europe between 65 and 60 million years ago, before spreading across the globe.  

The research indicates that flight and echolocation emerged near the beginning of bat evolution. These early adaptations may help explain how bats became one of the most successful mammal groups on Earth.
summary: A genomic and fossil study indicates bats first evolved in Europe around 65 to 60 million years ago before spreading across the globe. The findings also suggest flight and echolocation emerged near the beginning of bat evolution, helping explain how bats became one of the most successful mammal groups on Earth.
author: Science Daily

title: Blacktip Sharks Detect Low-Frequency Sounds from 250 Feet Away
content: Wild blacktip sharks can detect low‑frequency sounds from nearly 250 feet away, researchers found in experiments conducted off the Florida coast. The study showed that the sharks not only heard the sounds but sharply changed direction away from them, indicating they could pinpoint the source of the noise.
summary: Wild blacktip sharks can detect low-frequency sounds from nearly 250 feet away, according to experiments off the Florida coast. The sharks also changed direction sharply away from the sounds, indicating they can pinpoint the source.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists crack 25-year challenge to identify W states in quantum entanglement
content:
Scientists have developed and experimentally demonstrated a long‑sought method for identifying W states, a key form of multi‑photon quantum entanglement. The new technique addresses a 25‑year challenge in the field of quantum physics.  

By enabling easier measurement of complex entangled systems, the method could expand the practical use of quantum teleportation, communication, and computing. The breakthrough offers a new tool for researchers working with multi‑photon entanglement.

title: Strata: New Semantic Layer Simplifies LLM Integration
content:
Ajo, who spent four years at Netflix working on self-service solutions for non-technical business users, has introduced Strata, an expressive semantic layer designed to work with large language models. The full-stack solution includes dashboards, subscriptions, and Google Sheets exports, accessible via view agent conversations or Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Key features of Strata include strict naming conventions that ensure only one entity, such as "Revenue," exists per project, enabling automatic data blending across fact domains. The system utilizes partition and aggregate-aware semantic routing to select faster compute engines like Druid or ClickHouse for specific queries while retaining full history in cheaper engines like Trino. Additional capabilities include out-of-the-box support for complex measures like snapshots, LOD, and compound measures, as well as the ability to create custom calculations and apply cohorts as filters.

Strata is currently in early beta and is not open source, though it offers a free tier supporting up to 25 users that can be run locally via Docker. The developer explicitly states they are not building a semantic layer for traditional BI tools, instead providing APIs and MCP for custom integrations.
summary: Ajo, who spent four years at Netflix building self‑service tools for non‑technical users, built Strata, a full‑stack semantic layer that balances expressiveness and ease of use and works well with LLMs. Strata offers dashboards, subscriptions, Google Sheets exports, strict naming conventions, automatic data blending, tiered compute routing, complex measures, custom calculations, cohort filtering, and can be accessed via agent conversation or via MCP, and is available as an early beta that is not open source but includes a free tier for up to 25 users that can run on Docker.

title: Magnitude (YC S25) Launches Self-Optimizing Inference Engine for Local Agents
content:
Launch HN: Magnitude (YC S25) – Self‑optimizing inference engine for agents

Anders and Tom, software engineers who previously built an open‑source browser agent with 4,000+ GitHub stars and 100,000+ downloads, have announced Magnitude, a new inference engine that automatically tunes itself to run as fast as possible on a user’s hardware. The engine supports Mac, Linux, and Windows on any hardware and claims to be up to twice as fast as llama.cpp.

Magnitude is designed for local agent workloads, offering on‑device kernel compilation and tuning, focus on popular open‑weight families, dynamic memory allocation that grows only as needed, and hybrid paged attention that shares prefix caches without sacrificing single‑session speed. Benchmarks with the Qwen 3.6 35B A3B (4‑bit) model show a 92 % faster decode on a Mac M4 Pro (30 tok/s → 57 tok/s) and a 19 % faster decode on a DGX Spark GPU (49 tok/s → 58 tok/s), along with 27–28 % less per‑agent memory usage.

The project is fully open source under the Apache 2.0 license, built in Rust with a custom GPU kernel runtime and autotuner. Future plans include expert streaming, a kernel compiler for automatic fusion, and multi‑device utilization. The team invites users to try the desktop app, connect it to agents such as Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, and Codex, and provide feedback via the comments link.
summary: Magnitude is an open-source inference engine built in Rust that optimizes itself for specific hardware to run local agents up to 2x faster than llama.cpp. It features dynamic memory allocation and hybrid paged attention to allow concurrent sessions without sacrificing single-session performance.

content:

Muse’s capabilities extend beyond basic tasks. Meta has made the agent’s filesystem more accessible, allowing users to download its entire contents, and plans to add video‑chat functionality. The company is also developing a Tamagotchi‑style Muse Charm device that will not include Instagram integration but can interact with other Muse Charms. In addition, Muse is slated for integration with Meta smart glasses and a standalone gadget, and the platform’s Enterprise version will bring Muse AI tools to small businesses.

The launch has sparked security concerns, as Muse was reported to have sent a YouTuber’s address to a stranger and an exploit that could let attackers control the agent. Meta patched the vulnerability, but Amazon has blocked the Muse AI agent, and Mark Zuckerberg has urged users to trust the system. Muse now also has a Mac app, and Meta continues to position the agent as a key player in its AI strategy.
summary: Meta launched Muse AI, an agent that can send emails and handle online purchases, and has added new features such as a Muse Charm device and a Mac app. The company also patched a security exploit that allowed attackers to control the AI agent.
